norms.heading: Substitution of parties upon death, mental incapacity or transfer of interest.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. (1) If a party dies and the claim is not thereby extinguished, the court shall on motion order substitution of the proper parties. The motion for substitution may be made by the successors or representatives of the deceased party or by any party and, together with the notice of the hearing, shall be served on the parties as provided in section 506.100, and upon persons not parties in the manner provided for the service of a summons.

(2) In the event of the death of one or more of the plaintiffs or of one or more of the defendants in an action in which the right sought to be enforced survives only to the surviving plaintiffs or only against the surviving defendants, the action does not abate. The death shall be suggested upon the record and the action shall proceed in favor of or against the surviving parties.

(3) If the death occurs prior to final judgment or after final judgment and before appeal and substitution or motion therefor is not made within nine months after the first published notice of letters testamentary or of administration, the action shall be dismissed as to the deceased party; if death occurs after appeal and before final determination thereof and substitution or motion therefor is not made in the appellate court where the appeal is pending within nine months after the first published notice of letters testamentary or of administration, the appeal shall be dismissed as to the deceased party.

2. If a party becomes mentally incapacitated, the court upon motion served as provided in subsection 1 may allow the action to be continued by or against his representative.

3. In case of any transfer of interest, the action may be continued by or against the original party, unless the court upon motion directs the person to whom the interest is transferred to be substituted in the action or joined with the original party. Service of the motion shall be made as provided in subsection 1.

4. When a corporation has been sued and served with process or has appeared while in being, and is thereafter dissolved or its charter forfeited, the action shall not be affected thereby and any judgment obtained shall have the effect of a judgment against the last board of directors, in a representative capacity, although the members of the board were not joined in the action.

5. When any public officer is a party to an action and during its pendency dies, resigns, or otherwise ceases to hold office, the action may be continued and maintained by or against his successor upon motion made within one year. Before a substitution is made, the party or officer to be affected, unless expressly assenting thereto, shall be given reasonable notice of the application therefor and accorded an opportunity to object. If no successor is otherwise appointed or elected, the court in which the action is pending may appoint a successor for the prosecution or defense of the action.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 370 prévoit l’interruption, après notification, en cas de décès transmissible, de cessation du représentant légal ou de modification de la capacité d’ester. Les règles 52.13 et RSMo 507.100 organisent plutôt la substitution ou la continuation de l’instance, avec motion et délais; Rule 52.02 encadre la représentation des mineurs.
correspondences.note_en: Article 370 interrupts the action, after notice, for a transmissible death, loss of a legal representative, or a change in capacity to litigate. Rule 52.13 and RSMo 507.100 instead provide for substitution or continuation by motion and subject to deadlines; Rule 52.02 governs minor representation.

correspondences.note_fr: L’instance peut être reprise volontairement selon les formes des moyens de défense ou, à défaut, par citation. Rule 52.13 et RSMo 507.100 prévoient une reprise par motion et notification, avec service comme une assignation dans certains cas, mais sans mécanisme identique de reprise volontaire ou subsidiaire.
correspondences.note_en: The action may be voluntarily resumed through the forms for presenting defenses or, failing that, by citation. Rule 52.13 and RSMo 507.100 provide continuation by motion and notice, with summons-like service in some cases, but not the same voluntary/default resumption mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Après la reprise, l’instance continue dans l’état où elle se trouvait lors de l’interruption. Rule 52.13 et RSMo 507.100 permettent la continuation de l’action après décès, incapacité ou transfert, mais ne formulent pas expressément cette règle générale de reprise au même état procédural.
correspondences.note_en: After resumption, the action continues in the procedural state existing at interruption. Rule 52.13 and RSMo 507.100 permit continuation after death, incapacity, or transfer, but do not expressly state this general same-state resumption rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 531 interrompt le délai de recours lors d’un changement de capacité ou de certaines procédures collectives, puis le fait courir à compter d’une notification au nouveau destinataire. La Rule 52.13(g), avec les règles de substitution de la Rule 52.13 et du RSMo 507.100, retarde certains délais après jugement jusqu’à la substitution, mais ne reprend pas toutes ces hypothèses.
correspondences.note_en: Article 531 interrupts the appeal period after a change in capacity or certain insolvency proceedings and restarts it upon notice to the person entitled to receive notice. Rule 52.13(g), together with the substitution provisions in Rule 52.13 and RSMo 507.100, delays certain post-judgment periods until substitution, but does not cover all those events.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 532 interrompt le délai de recours au décès, puis prévoit une nouvelle notification au domicile du défunt ou aux héritiers, avec un point de départ lié aux délais successoraux. La Rule 52.13(a) et le RSMo 507.100 organisent la substitution après décès et ses délais, mais selon des mécanismes et délais différents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 532 interrupts the appeal period upon death and provides for renewed notice at the decedent’s domicile or to the heirs, with timing linked to estate-inventory periods. Rule 52.13(a) and RSMo 507.100 govern substitution after death and related deadlines, but use materially different mechanisms and periods.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet de notifier le recours au domicile du défunt et collectivement à ses héritiers, mais exige que chacun soit cité avant qu’un jugement puisse être requis contre eux. Le Missouri prévoit la notification malgré le décès, la substitution et, dans certains cas, la poursuite ou la reprise du jugement contre les héritiers, sans reprendre exactement cette procédure.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits notice of an appeal at the deceased party’s domicile and collectively to heirs, but requires each heir to be summoned before judgment may be sought against them. Missouri addresses notice despite death, substitution, and in some cases continuation or revival against heirs, but not through the same procedure.

norms.heading: Suits by infants, how prosecuted.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: Suits by infants may only be commenced and prosecuted, either: First, by a duly appointed guardian or conservator of such infant; or, second, by a next friend appointed for him in such suit; or, third, if asserted by counterclaim, by a guardian ad litem.

norms.heading: Infant defined for civil suit purposes.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: As used in sections 507.110 to 507.220, the term "infant" means any person who has not attained the age of eighteen years. All persons of the age of eighteen years or older, not otherwise disqualified, may commence, prosecute, or defend any action in his own name as the real party in interest.
revisor_notes: (1979) Statute is to be construed to mean persons who have not attained age of 18 years. Holoman v. Harris (A.), 585 S.W.2d 530.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 369 prévoit plusieurs causes d’interruption automatique, dont la majorité et certains jugements d’insolvabilité. Les textes du Missouri traitent de la capacité et de la représentation des mineurs, ainsi que d’un sursis lié à la désignation d’un receiver, sans reprendre cette règle d’interruption automatique ni la cessation de fonctions de l’avocat.
correspondences.note_en: Article 369 provides several grounds for automatic interruption, including attaining majority and certain insolvency judgments. The Missouri texts address capacity and representation of minors and a receiver-related stay, but do not reproduce the automatic interruption rule or interruption caused by loss of counsel.

norms.heading: Appointment of next friend, by whom.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: The appointment of a next friend for an infant shall be made by the court in which the suit is intended to be brought, or by a judge or clerk thereof.

norms.heading: How appointed.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: Such appointment shall be made on the petition in writing of such infant, if of the age of fourteen years, and the written consent of the person proposed to be next friend to such infant acknowledged before, or proved to the court or officer making the appointment.

norms.heading: Appointment when minor is under fourteen years old.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: If such infant be under the age of fourteen years, the appointment of a next friend may be made upon like petition of a relative or friend of the infant, in which case a notice thereof must first be given to the person with whom such infant resides.

norms.heading: Bond of person acting for infant, when — effect of failure to give.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. Before a next friend or guardian ad litem can receive or receipt for any money or property, personal or real, and before he can acknowledge satisfaction or discharge of any judgment, he must execute a bond to such infant; except, that no bond shall be required if the total value of the property or money, exclusive of expenses and fees approved by the court, is not in excess of ten thousand dollars and all of the money or property is to be turned over to the infant or his parent. The bond must be approved by the court or the clerk thereof and shall be conditioned that the next friend or guardian ad litem shall account to the infant for all money or property which has or does come into his hands, less only those expenses and attorney fees the payment of which has been approved by order of the court. The bond shall be in an amount equal to the value of the money or property if the surety is a corporate bonding, surety or insurance company, and in an amount double the value of the money or property if the surety is not a corporate bonding, surety or insurance company, in which event there shall be two sureties. In either event, the surety or sureties shall be approved by the court or clerk thereof before the bond can be approved.

2. Failure to execute such approved bond with approved surety or sureties when required under the provisions of subsection 1 of this section shall, upon receipt by a next friend or guardian ad litem of any money or property for or on behalf of such minor, immediately render such next friend or guardian ad litem personally liable to the minor for a penal sum in an amount double the value of the money or property and also shall render absolutely void and of no effect any release, receipt or acknowledgment of satisfaction or discharge of any judgment which has or is in the future made or executed by the next friend or guardian ad litem.

3. The next friend's duties or guardian ad litem's duties and his obligations under the bond shall continue until he is discharged therefrom by order of the court.

norms.heading: Bond filed, where.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: Such bond shall be delivered to such officer before the appointment shall be made, and shall be filed in the office of the clerk of the court in which the suit is to be brought.

norms.heading: Petition and appointment filed before further proceedings.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: The petition for the appointment of a next friend, the written consent of the person proposed to be next friend, and the order of appointment, shall be filed in the office of the clerk of the court where the suit is proposed to be brought, before any proceedings shall be had in the cause.

norms.heading: Guardian, conservator and next friend liable for costs.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: The guardian, conservator, or next friend of any infant who commences or prosecutes a suit shall be responsible for the costs thereof, unless such infant be permitted by the court to sue as a poor person, as provided by law.

norms.heading: Next friend, conservator, or guardian may employ attorney and incur expenses.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: The next friend, guardian ad litem or guardian or conservator shall have authority without an order of court to contract for and employ an attorney upon a reasonable fee, including one contingent upon the outcome of such action or claim, and to incur reasonable expenses in the preparation and prosecution of such action or claim, but any such fee and expenses shall be subject to the approval of the court, but if approved by the court shall be payable out of any money or property recovered or obtained in the prosecution or settlement of such action, claim or any judgment thereon.

norms.heading: Powers of next friend, GAL, conservator or guardian on trial and settlement — court approval — settlement of claims permitted.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. The next friend, guardian ad litem or guardian or conservator shall have the power and authority, subject to the approval of the court, to waive a jury and submit all issues in such action or proposed settlement to the court for determination.

2. The next friend, guardian ad litem or guardian or conservator shall have the power and authority to contract on behalf of the minor for a settlement of the minor's claim, action or judgment, provided that such contract and settlement shall not be effective until approved by the court. The next friend, guardian ad litem and guardian or conservator shall also have the power and authority to execute and sign a release or satisfaction and discharge of a judgment which shall be binding upon the minor, provided the court orders the execution of such release or satisfaction and discharge of judgment.

3. The court shall have the power and authority to hear evidence on and either approve or disapprove a proposed contract to settle an action or claim of a minor, to authorize and order the next friend, guardian ad litem or guardian or conservator to execute and sign a release or satisfaction and discharge of judgment, and shall also have the power and authority to approve a fee contract between the next friend, guardian ad litem or guardian or conservator and an attorney and to order him to pay an attorney fee and to pay the expenses which have been reasonably incurred in connection with the preparation and prosecution of the action or claim and including the cost of any bonds required herein.

4. Notwithstanding the provisions of this section to the contrary, nothing in this section shall be construed as prohibiting the settlement of claims pursuant to section 436.700 or as requiring court approval of settlements pursuant to section 436.700.
revisor_notes: (1973) Judicial settlement of claim against tort-feasors does not release contractual liability of insuror to pay medical expenses to minor not a party to insurance contract. Aetna Casualty and Surety Co. v. Bailey (A.), 497 S.W.2d 816.
(1979) Statute is to be construed to mean persons who have not attained age of 18 years. Holoman v. Harris (A.), 585 S.W.2d 530.

(1981) Judgment entered under provisions of statute for the purpose of effecting a settlement of a minor's cause of action does not bar subsequent suit against persons who were not parties to the action. Arthur v. Evangelical Deaconess Society, etc. (A.), 615 S.W.2d 438.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge chargé d’une mesure d’instruction peut homologuer l’accord mettant fin au litige. La Rule 52.08(e) et le RSMo 507.184 prévoient une approbation judiciaire de certains règlements, mais dans des contextes limités; la Rule 84.02 permet seulement d’explorer un règlement en appel.
correspondences.note_en: The judge overseeing an evidentiary measure may approve an agreement ending the dispute. Rule 52.08(e) and RSMo 507.184 require court approval for certain settlements, but only in limited contexts; Rule 84.02 merely permits settlement exploration on appeal.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 This is the same as Rule 23 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 281 prévoit qu’en cas de conciliation pendant l’expertise, l’expert constate que sa mission est devenue sans objet et en informe le juge; les parties peuvent demander que leur accord reçoive force exécutoire. La Rule 88.08 organise un accord écrit issu d’une médiation et son exécution, tandis que les deux sections RSMo prévoient, dans des contextes particuliers, l’approbation ou l’exécution judiciaire d’un règlement.
correspondences.note_en: Article 281 provides that, when the parties settle during the expert process, the expert reports that the mission has become moot; the parties may ask the judge to make their agreement enforceable. Rule 88.08 governs a written mediation settlement and its enforcement, while the two RSMo sections provide court approval or judgment enforcement of settlements in specialized contexts.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 384 prévoit l’extinction accessoire de l’instance par transaction, acquiescement, désistement d’action ou décès dans les actions non transmissibles, constatée par une décision de dessaisissement. Les règles du Missouri traitent surtout du désistement volontaire, de ses effets, du décès d’une partie et, spécifiquement, de l’homologation des transactions concernant les mineurs; elles ne reprennent pas l’ensemble du mécanisme français.
correspondences.note_en: Article 384 provides for incidental termination of the proceeding through settlement, acquiescence, withdrawal of the claim, or death in non-transmissible actions, recorded by a decision divesting the court. Missouri provisions address voluntary dismissal and its effects, death of a party, and—specifically—court approval of minors’ settlements, but do not reproduce the full French mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Le mandat de représentation est réputé conférer au représentant un pouvoir spécial pour accomplir certains actes procéduraux, notamment le désistement, l’acquiescement, les offres, l’aveu et le consentement. La Rule 55.035 reconnaît une représentation générale, tandis que RSMo 507.184 confère seulement certaines prérogatives de règlement aux représentants de mineurs ou incapables, sous contrôle judiciaire.
correspondences.note_en: The article deems a litigation representative to have special authority for withdrawal, acquiescence, offers, admissions, and consent. Rule 55.035 recognizes general representation, while RSMo 507.184 grants only limited settlement-related powers to representatives of minors or incapacitated persons, subject to court approval.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge homologue l’accord que les parties lui soumettent selon les conditions prévues par le texte référencé. Les textes du Missouri prévoient une approbation judiciaire expresse de certains règlements, notamment en matière de confiscation et de demandes de mineurs.
correspondences.note_en: The French judge approves the agreement submitted by the parties under the conditions of the referenced provision. The Missouri texts require express court approval of certain settlements, notably forfeiture matters and minors’ claims.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge homologue l’accord soumis par les parties. La Rule 88.08 rend un accord écrit de médiation obligatoire sans homologation judiciaire, tandis que RSMo 507.184 prévoit l’approbation judiciaire de certains règlements, notamment ceux concernant les mineurs.
correspondences.note_en: The judge approves an agreement submitted by the parties. Rule 88.08 makes a written mediation settlement binding without judicial approval, while RSMo 507.184 requires court approval for certain settlements, particularly claims involving minors.

correspondences.note_fr: L’homologation est demandée par requête par les parties ou la plus diligente devant le juge compétent, avec décision en principe sans débat. RSMo 513.617 et 507.184 exigent l’approbation judiciaire de certains règlements, mais dans des matières particulières; RSMo 511.740 prévoit une soumission consensuelle au tribunal, avec audition obligatoire.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits the parties, or the more diligent party, to request approval before the seized or otherwise competent judge, normally without a hearing. RSMo 513.617 and 507.184 require court approval of specified settlements, while RSMo 511.740 allows consensual submission to a competent court but requires a hearing.

norms.heading: Substitution of conservator for next friend or guardian ad litem — effect of contracts.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. At any time during the preparation or prosecution of such action or claim, before or after judgment or appeal, the minor's duly appointed conservator may be substituted for the next friend or guardian ad litem. The substitution may be made by the court or the clerk thereof upon an ex parte showing of the appointment and qualification of the conservator. In the event of such substitution, the court shall, upon payment or transfer of all of the minor's money or property in his hands to the conservator and filing a receipt for the same with a certified copy of the conservator's letters attached to it, and acceptance of the receipt by the court or clerk thereof as authentic, discharge the next friend or guardian ad litem from all of his obligations and duties as such.

2. In the event the minor's conservator has been substituted for the next friend or guardian ad litem and the attorney fees and expenses have not, at the time of the substitution, been paid, the conservator shall be bound by the attorney fee contract and shall be obligated to pay the attorney fees and expenses to the same extent as the next friend or guardian ad litem would have been obligated to pay them had he not been discharged, provided the attorney fees and expenses are approved by the court.

correspondences.note_fr: Le § 507.186 RSMo prévoit, dans le remplacement d’un représentant d’un mineur, le transfert des biens ou fonds au conservateur et la décharge de l’ancien représentant. Il ne traite ni l’action de groupe ni le mandat ou la substitution d’un demandeur défaillant.
correspondences.note_en: RSMo 507.186 provides, when replacing a minor’s representative, for transferring money or property to the conservator and discharging the former representative. It does not address group actions, mandates, or substitution of a defaulting claimant.

norms.heading: Disposition of proceeds of claim — discharge of next friend or guardian ad litem.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. If, after paying the attorney fee and the expenses, the next friend or guardian ad litem has in his hands money or property of the minor in an amount equal to or less than ten thousand dollars, then the court may, if in its discretion it finds it to be to the best interests of the minor to do so, order the next friend or guardian ad litem to pay, deposit, or deliver all or any part of such money or property in accordance with one of the alternatives prescribed by subsection 1 of section 475.330. The provisions of chapters 473 and 475 shall apply to any such payment, deposit, or delivery. In the event of such order and payment, deposit, or delivery, the next friend or guardian ad litem shall file with the court or the clerk thereof a receipt from the person to whom the payment, deposit, or delivery was made evidencing such payment, deposit, or delivery. After such receipt has been filed and accepted by the court or clerk thereof as authentic, then the court or clerk thereof may order the next friend or guardian ad litem discharged and released from all of his duties and obligations and from his bond. In the event such payment or delivery is to the minor, then the minor's signature upon the receipt shall be unavoidable, irrevocable and forever binding upon the minor.

2. If, after paying the attorney fee and the expenses, the next friend or guardian ad litem has in his hands money or property of the minor in an amount in excess of ten thousand dollars, then the court shall order the next friend or guardian ad litem to pay or transfer such money or property to a duly appointed and qualified conservator of the minor. Upon such payment or transfer, the next friend or guardian ad litem shall file with the court or the clerk thereof a receipt from such conservator to whom such payment or transfer was made, evidencing such payment, with a certified copy of such conservator's letters attached to such receipt. After such receipt has been filed and accepted by the court as authentic, then the court shall order the next friend or guardian ad litem discharged and released from all of his duties and obligations and from his bond.

norms.heading: Suits against infants not to proceed without guardian ad litem.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: After the commencement of a suit against an infant defendant, and the service of process upon him, the suit shall not be prosecuted any further until a guardian ad litem for such infant be appointed.

norms.heading: Appointment of guardian ad litem.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: The appointment of a guardian ad litem shall be made by the court in which the suit is pending, or by the judge thereof in vacation, upon the written request of the infant defendant, if of the age of fourteen years or more, or, if such infant be under said age, on the written request of a relative or friend of the infant, and on the written consent of any competent person proposed as guardian ad litem, and such request and consent shall be filed in the office of the clerk of the court before any answer by such infant shall be filed.

norms.heading: Appointment of guardian ad litem, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: If such infant defendant neglects, for one day after the expiration of the time within which the infant defendant is summoned to appear to the suit, to procure the appointment of a guardian ad litem to defend the suit, the court shall appoint some competent person to be guardian ad litem for such infant in the defense of such suit.

norms.heading: Guardian ad litem, liable only for costs in case of misconduct.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text: No person appointed guardian ad litem for an infant, for the purpose of defending a suit against such infant, shall be liable for the costs of such suit, unless specially charged by the order of the court for some personal misconduct in such cause.

norms.heading: Who made defendants in suit against city.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 507 Parties

norms.text:
1. Whenever a city of over one hundred and fifty thousand inhabitants shall be sued in any court in this state and the cause of action on account of which said city is sued shall arise from the wrongful or unauthorized acts or carelessness and negligence of any person or corporation subject to service in this state, and such wrongful or unauthorized acts or carelessness and negligence shall also make such person or corporation liable to an action by the plaintiff on the same account as such city is sued for, such city may, within fifteen days after the first day of the next term of court after the service of the writ of summons, file a motion, in writing, in said case, notifying the plaintiff therein to make such person or corporation a party defendant in said suit in accordance with the facts constituting the liability of such person or corporation, which facts said city shall set forth in said notice, and shall verify the same by affidavit.

2. The plaintiff in said suit shall then proceed to join such person or corporation as a party defendant in said suit, in accordance with the facts set forth in said notice, and such suit shall not be prosecuted against said city until such person or corporation is made a codefendant with such city; provided, however, that in case the facts set forth in said notice do not make such person or corporation named therein liable to an action on the same account as such city is sued for in such case, said plaintiff may file a motion to strike out said notice, and if said motion shall be sustained by the court, then the plaintiff in such case may proceed against defendant city alone, as if said notice had not been filed; and provided further, that if the plaintiff shall make such person or corporation as may be named in said notice a party defendant in said suit and shall have caused summons to be issued for such person or corporation, and such person or corporation cannot be served with process by the officer to whom such writ is directed, then the plaintiff in such case may proceed against the city alone.

norms.heading: Venue for nontort and tort suits.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text:
1. (1) As used in this section, "principal place of residence" shall mean the county which is the main place where an individual resides in the state of Missouri. There shall be only one principal place of residence.

(2) For an individual person, there shall be a rebuttable presumption that the county of voter registration at the time of injury is the principal place of residence.

(3) Notwithstanding subdivision (2) of this subsection, for an individual whose conduct at issue was alleged in at least one count to be in the course and scope of his or her employment with a corporation, the individual's principal place of residence for venue purposes shall be deemed to be the applicable corporation's principal place of residence.

(4) For a corporation that, either directly or through its subsidiaries, wholly owns or operates a railroad, the place where the corporation has its registered agent is its principal place of residence for the purposes of venue, provided that the registered agent is in a city not within a county, a charter county, or a first class county.

2. In all actions in which there is no count alleging a tort, venue shall be determined as follows:

(1) When the defendant is a resident of the state, either in the county within which the defendant resides, or in the county within which the plaintiff resides, and the defendant may be found;

(2) When there are several defendants, and they reside in different counties, the suit may be brought in any such county;

(3) When there are several defendants, some residents and others nonresidents of the state, suit may be brought in any county in this state in which any defendant resides;

(4) When all the defendants are nonresidents of the state, suit may be brought in any county in this state, provided there is personal jurisdiction over each defendant, independent of each other defendant.

3. The term "tort" shall include claims based upon improper health care, under the provisions of chapter 538.

4. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, in all actions in which there is any count alleging a tort and in which the plaintiff was first injured in the state of Missouri, venue shall be in the county where the plaintiff was first injured by the acts or conduct alleged in the action.

5. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, in all actions in which there is any count alleging a tort and in which the plaintiff was first injured outside the state of Missouri, venue as to that individual plaintiff shall be determined as follows:

(1) If the defendant is a corporation, then venue shall be in any county where a defendant corporation's registered agent is located or, if the plaintiff's principal place of residence was in the state of Missouri on the date the plaintiff was first injured, then venue may be in the county of the plaintiff's principal place of residence on the date the plaintiff was first injured;

(2) If the defendant is an individual, then venue shall be in the county where the defendant has his or her principal place of residence in the state of Missouri, which for venue purposes shall be deemed to be that of his or her employer corporation if any count alleges conduct in the course and scope of his or her employment with that corporation, or, if the plaintiff's principal place of residence was in the state of Missouri on the date the plaintiff was first injured, then venue as to that individual plaintiff may be in the county containing the plaintiff's principal place of residence on the date the plaintiff was first injured;

(3) Notwithstanding subdivisions (1) and (2) of this subsection, if the plaintiff was first injured in a foreign country in connection with any railroad operations therein and any defendant is a:

(a) Corporation that, either directly or through its subsidiaries, wholly owns or operates the foreign railroad; or

(b) Wholly owned subsidiary of a corporation that, either directly or through its subsidiaries, wholly owns or operates the foreign railroad;

then venue shall exclusively be in the county where any such defendant corporation's registered agent is located, regardless of venue as to any other defendant or, if the plaintiff's principal place of residence was in the state of Missouri on the date the plaintiff was first injured, then venue may be in the county of the plaintiff's principal place of residence on the date the plaintiff was first injured.

6. Any action, in which any county shall be a plaintiff, may be commenced and prosecuted to final judgment in the county in which the defendant or defendants reside, or in the county suing and where the defendants, or one of them, may be found.

7. In all actions, process shall be issued by the court in which the action is filed and process may be served in any county within the state.

8. In any action for defamation or for invasion of privacy, the plaintiff shall be considered first injured in the county in which the defamation or invasion was first published.

9. In all actions, venue shall be determined as of the date the plaintiff was first injured.

10. All motions to dismiss or to transfer based upon a claim of improper venue shall be deemed granted if not denied within ninety days of filing of the motion unless such time period is waived in writing by all parties.

11. In a wrongful death action, the plaintiff shall be considered first injured where the decedent was first injured by the wrongful acts or negligent conduct alleged in the action. In any spouse's claim for loss of consortium, the plaintiff claiming consortium shall be considered first injured where the other spouse was first injured by the wrongful acts or negligent conduct alleged in the action.

12. The provisions of this section shall apply irrespective of whether the defendant is a for-profit or a not-for-profit entity.

13. In any civil action, if all parties agree in writing to a change of venue, the court shall transfer venue to the county within the state unanimously chosen by the parties. If any parties are added to the cause of action after the date of said transfer who do not consent to said transfer then the cause of action shall be transferred to such county in which venue is appropriate under this section, based upon the amended pleadings.

14. A plaintiff is considered first injured where the trauma or exposure occurred rather than where symptoms are first manifested.

15. If the county where the plaintiff's claim is filed is not a proper venue, that plaintiff shall be transferred to a county where proper venue can be established. If no such county exists in the state of Missouri, the claim shall be dismissed without prejudice.

16. Denial of a motion to transfer venue pursuant to section* 507.040, 507.050, or 508.010, if denied in error, requires reversal, and no finding of prejudice under Missouri supreme court rule 84.13(b) is required for reversal.

17. For the purposes of this section, a domestic insurance company shall be deemed to reside in, and be a resident of, the county where its registered office is maintained. A foreign insurance company shall be deemed to reside in, and be a resident of, the county where its registered office is maintained. If a foreign insurance company does not maintain a registered office in any county in Missouri, the foreign insurance company shall be deemed to reside in, and be a resident of, Cole County.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 42 fixe le for général au domicile du défendeur, avec des options en cas de pluralité de défendeurs ou d’absence de domicile connu. Le RSMo 508.010 règle aussi le venue selon la résidence du défendeur et prévoit des règles pour les défendeurs multiples, mais selon des conditions distinctes, notamment pour les actions délictuelles.
correspondences.note_en: Article 42 establishes the general venue at the defendant’s residence, with alternatives for multiple defendants or an unknown residence. RSMo 508.010 likewise governs venue by defendant residence and multiple defendants, but under materially different conditions, especially for tort actions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 43 précise que le domicile du défendeur correspond au domicile ou à la résidence d’une personne physique, et au lieu d’établissement d’une personne morale. Le RSMo 508.010 utilise principalement la notion de résidence principale et contient certaines règles propres aux personnes morales, sans reprendre entièrement ces définitions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 43 defines the defendant’s location as the domicile or residence of an individual and the establishment of a legal entity. RSMo 508.010 mainly uses principal residence and contains certain entity-specific venue rules, but does not reproduce these definitions in full.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit plusieurs fors facultatifs selon la nature de l’action, notamment le contrat, le délit et l’immeuble. RSMo 508.010 règle principalement la venue des actions non délictuelles et délictuelles, tandis que RSMo 508.030 impose le comté de situation pour les actions immobilières, selon des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides optional venues based on the action’s nature, including contract, tort, and real estate claims. RSMo 508.010 addresses venue for nontort and tort actions, while RSMo 508.030 requires venue where real estate is located, but under materially different conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 77 autorise, dans certains cas, le relevé d'office de l'incompétence territoriale. La Rule 51.045 organise la demande de transfert pour improper venue, avec un délai et une renonciation ; RSMo 509.290 permet de soulever l'improper venue par motion ; RSMo 508.010 prévoit le transfert depuis un comté inapproprié, sans reprendre les distinctions françaises.
correspondences.note_en: Article 77 permits sua sponte territorial-jurisdiction review in specified proceedings. Rule 51.045 governs a motion to transfer for improper venue, including a deadline and waiver; RSMo 509.290 permits improper venue to be raised by motion; RSMo 508.010 provides transfer from an improper county without reproducing the French distinctions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 849 fixe la compétence territoriale au domicile du défendeur et attribue compétence au tribunal de Paris si le défendeur est à l’étranger ou sans domicile connu. RSMo 508.010 règle le venue selon la résidence des parties, mais prévoit de nombreuses règles alternatives et différentes selon la nature de l’action.
correspondences.note_en: Article 849 assigns venue to the defendant’s domicile and to Paris when the defendant is abroad or has no known residence. RSMo 508.010 governs venue by party residence, but supplies numerous alternative and claim-specific rules with materially different conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe le tribunal territorialement compétent selon le lieu de résidence de la personne concernée, avec compétence résiduelle du tribunal de Paris pour les personnes résidant hors de France. Le RSMo 508.010 règle la venue selon la résidence et d’autres facteurs, tandis que la Rule 51.045 organise le transfert en cas de venue impropre.
correspondences.note_en: The article determines territorial venue by the residence of the person whose nationality is disputed, with a residual Paris forum for persons living outside France. RSMo 508.010 uses residence and other factors to determine venue, while Rule 51.045 governs transfer when venue is improper.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1048 fixe les juridictions territorialement compétentes selon le domicile de la personne, le lieu de l’acte et certains services spécialisés. Le § 508.010 RSMo énonce des règles générales de venue, sans reprendre ces critères spéciaux ni les règles de compétence juridictionnelle.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1048 assigns territorial competence based on the person’s residence, the place of the act, and certain specialized services. RSMo 508.010 provides general venue rules but does not reproduce these special criteria or jurisdictional rules.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe les juridictions territorialement compétentes pour une demande spéciale de modification du sexe et, éventuellement, des prénoms, avec une règle particulière pour certaines personnes protégées. Le RSMo 508.010 règle la compétence territoriale générale des actions civiles, sans régime spécifique comparable.
correspondences.note_en: The article assigns territorial jurisdiction for a special application concerning sex-marker and possibly name changes, including a special rule for certain protected persons. RSMo 508.010 provides general civil venue rules, but no comparable proceeding-specific regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe la compétence territoriale du juge pour les demandes relatives à la présomption d’absence, selon la résidence de l’intéressé ou du demandeur. Le RSMo 508.010 traite également du venue, mais selon des règles générales applicables aux actions civiles et sans régime spécifique de l’absence.
correspondences.note_en: The article sets territorial jurisdiction for applications concerning presumed absence, based on the person’s residence or, failing that, the applicant’s residence. RSMo 508.010 also governs venue, but through general civil-action rules and without a specific absent-person regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1066 fixe une compétence territoriale spéciale pour la déclaration d’absence, fondée sur le domicile ou la dernière résidence de l’absent, puis sur le domicile du demandeur. Le RSMo 508.010 énonce des règles générales de venue, sans règle spécifique aux procédures d’absence.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1066 establishes special territorial venue for a declaration of absence, based on the absent person's residence or last residence, and alternatively the applicant's residence. RSMo 508.010 provides general venue rules and contains no absence-specific rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article encadre la procédure européenne des petits litiges et fixe, à défaut de précision, la compétence territoriale au lieu de résidence du défendeur. Le RSMo 508.010 règle également le venue selon la résidence des parties, mais ne prévoit ni cette procédure européenne ni cette règle spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs the European Small Claims Procedure and, absent further designation, assigns territorial jurisdiction based on the defendant’s residence. RSMo 508.010 also addresses venue based on party residence, but does not provide the European procedure or this specific rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe la compétence territoriale de la juridiction française lorsque le règlement européen désigne seulement l’État membre : lieu où demeure le défendeur. Le RSMo 508.010 prévoit aussi des règles de venue fondées sur la résidence du défendeur, mais dans un cadre plus large et avec des alternatives différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article fixes territorial jurisdiction, when the European regulation designates only the Member State, at the defendant’s place of residence. RSMo 508.010 also uses the defendant’s residence for venue, but in a broader framework with different alternatives.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article offre un choix de compétence territoriale entre le domicile du défendeur et le lieu d’exécution de l’obligation. RSMo 508.010 prévoit notamment le lieu de résidence du défendeur, mais pas le lieu d’exécution comme fondement général et organise différemment les autres hypothèses.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits venue either where the defendant resides or where the obligation is to be performed. RSMo 508.010 includes the defendant’s residence as a venue basis, but does not generally provide for the place of performance and uses different rules for other situations.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe des règles spéciales de compétence territoriale selon le lieu d’établissement de l’acte et le domicile du demandeur. RSMo 508.010 énonce des règles générales de venue, tandis que Rule 51.045 organise le transfert en cas de venue impropre, sans règle propre à la reconstitution d’actes.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes special territorial rules based on where the instrument was made and where the claimant resides. RSMo 508.010 provides general venue rules, while Rule 51.045 governs transfer for improper venue; neither contains the article’s action-specific rules.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1459 désigne le juge d’appui, fixe sa compétence territoriale et permet une désignation conventionnelle. RSMo 508.010 et la Rule 51.02 traitent du venue et de son transfert convenu, tandis que RSMo 515.030 prévoit la désignation judiciaire d’un referee, mais aucun texte ne règle spécifiquement le juge d’appui arbitral.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1459 identifies the supporting judge and sets territorial venue, including venue agreed by the parties. RSMo 508.010 and Rule 51.02 address venue and agreed transfers, while RSMo 515.030 provides court appointment of referees; none specifically governs an arbitral supporting judge.

norms.heading: Change of venue, state statute prevails if in conflict with supreme court rules.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: To the extent that rule 51.03 of the Missouri rules of civil procedure contradicts any provision of this chapter, the provisions of this chapter shall prevail regarding any tort claim.
revisor_notes: Applicability of statute changes to cases filed after August 28, 2005, 538.305

norms.heading: Transfer of case based on addition, removal or severance of a plaintiff or defendant prior to commencement of trial.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: At any time prior to the commencement of a trial, if a plaintiff or defendant, including a third-party plaintiff or defendant, is either added to, removed, or severed from a petition filed in any court in the state of Missouri which would have, if originally added to, removed, or severed from the initial petition, altered the determination of venue under section 508.010, then the judge shall upon application of any party transfer the case to a proper forum.
revisor_notes: Applicability of statute changes to cases filed after August 28, 2005, 538.305

norms.heading: Venue for actions filed after or pending as of February 13, 2019.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text:
1. The provisions of sections 507.040, 507.050, 508.010, 508.012, and 537.762 shall apply to any action filed after February 13, 2019. A plaintiff who is a resident of Missouri and who has a case that:

(1) Is pending in a court in this state as of February 13, 2019;

(2) Has proper jurisdiction in this state; and

(3) Has or had been set at any time prior to February 13, 2019, for a trial date beginning on or before August 28, 2019,

may continue to trial in the venue as filed.

2. For actions pending as of February 13, 2019, a plaintiff whose claim has been found to have no county in Missouri in which venue exists may proceed in such venue in Missouri where such claim was dismissed without prejudice only when the court finds that the claim:

(1) Was filed in the Missouri court within the statute of limitations applicable to the claim;

(2) Has no proper venue in the state of Missouri; and

(3) Cannot be maintained, as of August 28, 2019, in any state where the claim may be brought because of applicable statutes of limitations and lack of a savings statute or similar law.

norms.heading: Suits by attachment or replevin, where commenced.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: Suits commenced by attachment against the property of a person, or in replevin or claim and delivery of personal property, where the specific property is sought to be recovered, shall be brought in the county in which such property may be found; and in all cases where the defendant in actions in replevin or claim and delivery of personal property is a nonresident of the county in which the suit is brought, service shall be made on him as under like circumstances in suits by attachment.

norms.heading: Actions for real estate, where commenced.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: Suits for the possession of real estate, or whereby the title thereto may be affected, or for the enforcement of the lien of any special tax bill thereon, shall be brought in the county where such real estate, or some part thereof, is situated.
revisor_notes: (1975) In either, a suit for specific performance or a suit on a contract incidentally requiring a delivery of a deed, concerning land in Camden County, venue is in Camden County and Jackson County circuit court was without jurisdiction. State ex rel. Uskali v. Snodgrass (A.), 524 S.W.2d 888.
(1977) Venue for actions which affect title to real estate cannot be waived. Gorman v. State Highway Commission (A.), 552 S.W.2d 335.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 44 attribue une compétence exclusive au lieu de situation de l’immeuble pour les matières réelles immobilières. Le RSMo 508.030 impose ce lieu pour les actions de possession, de titre ou de privilège fiscal spécial, mais le texte fourni ne démontre pas une identité de champ.
correspondences.note_en: Article 44 assigns exclusive venue to the place where the immovable property is located for real-property actions. RSMo 508.030 requires that location for possession, title, or special-tax-lien actions, but the supplied text does not establish identical scope.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit plusieurs fors facultatifs selon la nature de l’action, notamment le contrat, le délit et l’immeuble. RSMo 508.010 règle principalement la venue des actions non délictuelles et délictuelles, tandis que RSMo 508.030 impose le comté de situation pour les actions immobilières, selon des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides optional venues based on the action’s nature, including contract, tort, and real estate claims. RSMo 508.010 addresses venue for nontort and tort actions, while RSMo 508.030 requires venue where real estate is located, but under materially different conditions.

norms.heading: Suits against municipal corporations, where commenced.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text:
Suits against municipal corporations as defendant or codefendant shall be commenced only in the county in which the municipal corporation is situated, or if the municipal corporation is situated in more than one county, then suits against the municipal corporation shall be commenced only in that county wherein the seat of government of the municipal corporation is situated; except that:

(1) Suits may be brought against a city containing more than four hundred thousand inhabitants in any county in which any part of the city is situated; and

(2) Suits in inverse condemnation or involving dangerous conditions of public property against a municipal corporation established under Article VI, Section 30(a) of the Missouri Constitution shall be brought only in the county where such land or any part thereof lies.
revisor_notes: (1982) University of Missouri is not a "municipal corporation" within the meaning of statute requiring that suits against a municipal corporation be brought only in the county in which it is located. State ex rel. Milham v. Rickhoff (Mo.), 633 S.W.2d 733.

(1985) Provisions for judicial review of contested cases under the Administrative Procedure and Review Act are specific and controlling as against the general venue statute for suits against municipal corporations. State ex rel. City of Springfield v. Crouch (Mo.App.), 687 S.W.2d 639.

norms.heading: Actions against counties, where instituted.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: All actions whatsoever against any county shall be commenced in the circuit court of such county, and prosecuted to final judgment and execution therein, unless removed by change of venue to some other county, in which case the action or actions so removed shall be prosecuted to final judgment and execution in the circuit court of such other county.
revisor_notes: (1971) Appeal to circuit court of St. Louis City from order of air pollution appeal board of St. Louis County was not an action against St. Louis County and jurisdiction was not controlled by this section. State ex rel. Union Election Co. v. Scott (A.), 470 S.W.2d 1.

norms.heading: Suits against issuers of bad checks to the department of revenue, where commenced, when commenced — notice of election of venue to be given, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text:
1. Civil and criminal suits against issuers of checks payable to the Missouri department of revenue which are returned because of insufficient funds or no account shall be commenced in either the county where the defendant resides or in the county wherein the seat of state government is found provided any such issuer shall be given thirty days to make any such check good before any action is commenced in a county other than that of the residence of the issuer.

2. Notice of this election of venue statute shall be given to all persons who write a check payable to the Missouri department of revenue which is returned for insufficient funds or no account prior to commencement of legal proceedings on the check.

norms.heading: Civil action, transfer of prohibited if result is application of foreign law.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: No state court, arbitration panel, tribunal, or administrative agency shall transfer any civil action if such transfer would result in the application of any other foreign law, as the term foreign law is defined in section 506.602, that would violate or likely violate fundamental rights, as the term fundamental rights is defined in section 506.602.

norms.heading: Removal of suits by consent.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: If at any time after the commencement of a suit the parties shall agree in writing, duly filed, upon any other county or court of competent jurisdiction, to which they desire the same to be removed, it shall, by order of the court, be removed accordingly to such county or court of competent jurisdiction; and the same proceedings shall be had in all respects for the removal of such cause as are provided by law in changes of venue in civil cases.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 48 frappe de nullité relative les clauses dérogeant à la compétence territoriale, sauf accord entre commerçants et stipulation très apparente. Les textes du Missouri permettent, sous des conditions différentes, le transfert d’une action par accord écrit ou stipulation déposée, sans établir la même règle générale sur les clauses attributives de compétence.
correspondences.note_en: Article 48 renders territorial-jurisdiction clauses ineffective unless all parties contracted as merchants and the clause was conspicuous. The Missouri provisions allow transfer by written agreement or filed stipulation under different conditions, but do not establish the same general rule governing jurisdiction clauses.

norms.heading: Judge disqualified — change of venue granted, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet le renvoi vers un ressort limitrophe lorsqu’un magistrat ou auxiliaire de justice est partie. RSMo 508.090 et 508.140 organisent la disqualification et le changement de venue pour partialité ou influence, tandis que les Rules 51.04 et 51.05 prévoient respectivement le changement de venue ou de juge, avec des déclencheurs différents.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits transfer to a neighboring jurisdiction when a judge or legal officer is a party. RSMo 508.090 and 508.140 address disqualification and venue changes for prejudice or influence, while Rules 51.04 and 51.05 provide venue or judge changes on different grounds and procedures.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 341 renvoie, pour les causes de récusation, à l’article L. 111-6 du code de l’organisation judiciaire. Les textes du Missouri énumèrent certaines causes de disqualification et prévoient le transfert ou la désignation d’un autre juge, mais les causes et mécanismes ne sont pas identiques.
correspondences.note_en: Article 341 refers the grounds for recusal to article L. 111-6 of the French Code of Judicial Organization. The Missouri provisions list certain disqualification grounds and provide for reassignment or appointment of another judge, but the grounds and mechanisms are not identical.

norms.heading: Judge disqualified without application, when — exception.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: If a judge is interested in the cause before him, or related to either party, or has been of counsel in the cause, the court, without application from either party, shall either call in another circuit judge to sit in the case, as authorized by Section 15 of Article V of the Constitution, or request the supreme court to transfer a judge to try the cause, as authorized by Section 6 of Article V of the Constitution, unless all the parties in the cause consent that such judge may sit in the trial thereof.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 341 renvoie, pour les causes de récusation, à l’article L. 111-6 du code de l’organisation judiciaire. Les textes du Missouri énumèrent certaines causes de disqualification et prévoient le transfert ou la désignation d’un autre juge, mais les causes et mécanismes ne sont pas identiques.
correspondences.note_en: Article 341 refers the grounds for recusal to article L. 111-6 of the French Code of Judicial Organization. The Missouri provisions list certain disqualification grounds and provide for reassignment or appointment of another judge, but the grounds and mechanisms are not identical.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 350 prévoit une procédure spéciale devant le premier président de la Cour de cassation pour récuser le premier président d’une cour d’appel ou renvoyer toute la cour pour suspicion légitime. Les textes du Missouri prévoient plutôt le transfert ou la réassignation lorsqu’un juge est disqualifié, sans cette procédure institutionnelle spéciale.
correspondences.note_en: Article 350 creates a special procedure before the first president of the Court of Cassation for challenging an appellate chief judge or seeking transfer of an entire appellate court. The Missouri provisions instead provide reassignment or transfer when a judge is disqualified, without the same institutional procedure.

norms.heading: Judge disqualified, case transferred to another division of court, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: In all circuits composed of a single county which have more than four hundred thousand inhabitants, and in which there are two or more judges, when legal objection is made to the circuit judge assigned to try any case, the case shall be transferred to another division of the circuit court presided over by a different judge. Only one application shall be made by the same party in the same case, and shall be made as to only one of the judges of the court.

norms.heading: Application for disqualification of judge or change of venue — contents.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: Any party, his agent or attorney, may present to the court, or judge thereof in vacation, a petition setting forth the cause of his application for disqualification of the judge or for a change of venue, and when he obtained his information and knowledge of the existence thereof; and he shall annex thereto an affidavit, made by himself, his agent or attorney, to the truth of the petition, and that affiant has just cause to believe that he cannot have a fair trial on account of the cause alleged. If the removal is asked because of objections to the inhabitants of the county, the application shall not include therein any other county than the one from which the change of venue is asked.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 342 impose de présenter la récusation ou le renvoi dès la connaissance de la cause et au plus tard avant la clôture des débats. Le RSMo 508.130 exige d’indiquer quand la cause a été connue, tandis que la Rule 51.05 fixe des délais pour le changement de juge, avec des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 342 requires recusal or transfer to be sought promptly after the grounds become known and no later than the close of argument. RSMo 508.130 requires the application to state when the grounds were discovered, while Rule 51.05 sets different deadlines for a change of judge.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 343 autorise la partie ou son mandataire à agir, exige un pouvoir spécial et impose un avocat dans certaines juridictions. Le RSMo 508.130 permet également à la partie, à son agent ou à son avocat de présenter la demande, mais n’exige ni pouvoir spécial ni représentation obligatoire dans les mêmes termes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 343 permits the party or an agent to act, requires a special authority, and requires an attorney in specified courts. RSMo 508.130 likewise allows a party, agent, or attorney to file the application, but does not impose the same special-authority or mandatory-attorney requirements.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 344 fixe l’autorité saisie, les modalités de dépôt, le contenu obligatoire de la demande et les pièces justificatives. Le RSMo 508.130 exige une requête exposant le motif, la date de sa découverte et un affidavit; la Rule 51.05 prévoit une demande écrite, mais sans motif ni vérification pour le changement de juge de droit.
correspondences.note_en: Article 344 specifies the deciding authority, filing method, required grounds, and supporting documents. RSMo 508.130 requires a petition stating the cause, when it was learned, and an affidavit; Rule 51.05 requires a written application but generally dispenses with cause and verification for a change of judge.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose une présentation par avocat, l’énoncé des faits reprochés et la production des justificatifs. Les règles 94.03 et 97.03 exigent, pour des requêtes en mandamus ou prohibition, un exposé des faits et des pièces, tandis que l’article 508.130 exige une pétition et un affidavit, sans reprendre toutes ces conditions.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires filing by an attorney, a statement of the alleged facts, and supporting documents. Rules 94.03 and 97.03 require facts and exhibits for mandamus or prohibition petitions, while RSMo 508.130 requires a petition and affidavit but does not reproduce all these conditions.

norms.heading: After notice given, duty of court.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text:
1. If reasonable notice has been given to the adverse party or his attorney of record, the court or judge, as the case may be, shall consider the application, and if it is sufficient, the judge shall be disqualified or a change of venue shall be awarded to some county in the same, adjoining or next adjoining circuit, convenient to the parties for the trial of the case and where the causes complained of do not exist. One or more of several parties plaintiff or defendant may ask for the change of venue, and if the change is awarded the entire cause shall be removed, and there shall be no further change of venue awarded on the same side of the suit.

2. In all cases in counties in this state which have a population of more than sixty-five thousand inhabitants and wherein the removal is asked on the ground of objections to or prejudice of the inhabitants of the county and the adverse party has filed counter-affidavit controverting the objection to or the prejudice of the inhabitants of the county, the court shall hear evidence on the issue and determine the same on the merits of the evidence, and if the issue is determined in favor of the applicant for the change of venue, the change shall be awarded as herein provided.

3. This section does not apply to causes wherein a special venire has been issued, and in such case the party not applying for the special venire shall be granted a change of venue as of course, upon proper affidavit.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet le renvoi vers un ressort limitrophe lorsqu’un magistrat ou auxiliaire de justice est partie. RSMo 508.090 et 508.140 organisent la disqualification et le changement de venue pour partialité ou influence, tandis que les Rules 51.04 et 51.05 prévoient respectivement le changement de venue ou de juge, avec des déclencheurs différents.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits transfer to a neighboring jurisdiction when a judge or legal officer is a party. RSMo 508.090 and 508.140 address disqualification and venue changes for prejudice or influence, while Rules 51.04 and 51.05 provide venue or judge changes on different grounds and procedures.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 345 organise l’information du juge, les observations, l’abstention et l’absence d’effet suspensif, avec une suspension possible ordonnée par le premier président. Le RSMo 508.140 prévoit un avis à la partie adverse et l’examen de la demande; la Rule 51.05 organise ensuite le transfert et la réattribution, sans mécanisme correspondant de sursis.
correspondences.note_en: Article 345 governs notice to the judge, observations, recusal, the absence of an automatic stay, and a possible stay ordered by the chief judge. RSMo 508.140 provides notice and consideration of the application; Rule 51.05 provides transfer and reassignment, but not the corresponding stay mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 346 règle la décision rapide sur la récusation ou le renvoi, l’avis de la décision et le pourvoi contre le rejet. La Rule 51.05(e) impose la prise en compte rapide d’une demande de changement de juge et la réattribution; le RSMo 508.140 prévoit l’examen de la demande, mais aucun délai ni recours correspondant n’est fourni.
correspondences.note_en: Article 346 governs prompt disposition, notice of the decision, and review of a denial. Rule 51.05(e) requires prompt action on a change-of-judge application and reassignment; RSMo 508.140 provides consideration of the application, but the supplied texts contain no matching deadline or appeal.

norms.heading: Written order for change in vacation.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: If any judge award such change of venue in vacation, he shall immediately transmit to the clerk of the court wherein the cause is pending the petition and affidavit, with a written order for the change of venue.

norms.heading: Pleadings to be made up before award of change of venue.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: In all cases of application for a change of venue, all pleadings shall be filed and the issues made up before the entry awarding the change is made; but after the change of venue, any pleading found insufficient upon demurrer or otherwise may be amended as in other cases.

norms.heading: After change, clerk to transmit record.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: When any such order shall be made by the court or judge, the clerk shall immediately make out a full transcript of the record and proceedings in the cause, including the petition and affidavit and order of removal, and transmit the same, duly certified, together with all the original papers filed in the cause, and not forming a part of the record, to the clerk of the court to which the removal is ordered, and for failure to do so shall forfeit one hundred dollars to the party aggrieved, to be recovered by civil action.

correspondences.note_fr: Les textes du Missouri prévoient la transmission, le dépôt, l’enregistrement et l’avis aux avocats, mais les textes fournis ne prévoient ni invitation à poursuivre l’instance, ni délai de constitution, ni radiation pour défaut de constitution.
correspondences.note_en: The Missouri provisions provide for transmission, filing, docketing, and notice to counsel, but the supplied texts do not provide for an invitation to continue the action, an attorney-constitution deadline, or dismissal from the docket for failure to constitute counsel.

norms.heading: Clerk to file and docket cause when transmitted.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: The clerk of the court to which such cause is certified shall file the same, and the cause shall be docketed, proceeded in and determined as if it had originated therein.

correspondences.note_fr: Les textes du Missouri prévoient la transmission, le dépôt, l’enregistrement et l’avis aux avocats, mais les textes fournis ne prévoient ni invitation à poursuivre l’instance, ni délai de constitution, ni radiation pour défaut de constitution.
correspondences.note_en: The Missouri provisions provide for transmission, filing, docketing, and notice to counsel, but the supplied texts do not provide for an invitation to continue the action, an attorney-constitution deadline, or dismissal from the docket for failure to constitute counsel.

norms.heading: Party applying to pay costs, when — paid to which county — jury selection and service costs paid by county in which case originated.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text:
1. All the costs and expenses attending any such change of venue, made on the application of either party, shall be taxed against and paid by the petitioner, and shall not be taxed in the costs of the suit; provided, however, that when the change of venue is sought on the grounds of the prejudice of the inhabitants of the county, and the application is controverted by the opposing party, the costs incurred by the opposing party in hearing and determining said application shall be taxed against and paid by the losing party to said application.

2. All court costs paid or payable with respect to any civil case in which venue is transferred which are to be distributed to the county in which the case is filed, shall be paid to the county to which the case is transferred. If any such court costs have been paid by a party prior to the order changing venue, such costs shall be paid by the treasurer of the county in which the case was originally filed, to the county to which the case is transferred.

3. All expenses of whatever nature incurred by a county as a result of jury selection and service pursuant to the provisions of chapter 494 shall be paid by the county in which the case was originally instituted to the county in which the case is actually tried, except when such case is transferred for improper venue.

norms.heading: Failure of clerk to transmit, or loss of record, proceedings.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: If any clerk fail to transmit the transcript and papers in any cause, the venue whereof has been changed, or if they be sent and lost, such loss or failure shall not operate as a discontinuance of such cause, but they may be filed at the next term of said court; or, if lost, copies of the original may be furnished and filed, and the cause shall proceed as if no such failure or loss had happened; provided, however, that the court or the judge granting any change of venue shall have the power to set aside and annul the order thereof, by consent of parties, at any time before such transcript and papers shall be actually filed in such other court.

norms.heading: Jurisdiction of court in cases removed.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: The court to which any cause shall be transferred by change of venue shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine the same, and shall proceed to final judgment and execution therein; although such cause would not otherwise be cognizable in such court.

norms.heading: Change of venue from other counties.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: All causes in which a change of venue shall be awarded by the circuit court of any other county to the county of Cape Girardeau, the same may be certified and transferred to the circuit court of Cape Girardeau County at Jackson, or to the circuit court of Cape Girardeau County at Cape Girardeau, as may be directed by the court granting the change of venue, or by consent of parties, and whichever court shall receive the said cause shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine the same.

norms.heading: Further causes for change of venue.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.heading: Change of venue from district No. 2 of Marion County circuit court.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text:
1. Any case which may be pending in district number 2 of the circuit court of Marion County, Missouri, may be removed by change of venue for the following causes:

(1) That the inhabitants of Mason and Miller townships, Marion County, Missouri, are prejudiced against the applicant;

(2) That the opposite party has an undue influence over the inhabitants of said townships.

2. The change of venue may be awarded to any circuit court, including district number 1 of the circuit court of Marion County, Missouri, in the same manner that changes are taken from other circuit courts, and the court to which such cause may be removed shall have power and jurisdiction to dispose of the same as in causes taken by change of venue from circuit courts.

norms.heading: Change of venue to district No. 2 of Marion County circuit court.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text:
1. Except as otherwise specially provided by law, changes of venue in either civil or criminal cases may be awarded by any circuit court, including district number 1 of the circuit court of Marion County, Missouri, to district number 2 of the circuit court of Marion County, Missouri. Such changes of venue awarded by district number 1 of the circuit court of Marion County, Missouri, may be awarded for the following causes:

(1) That the inhabitants of all townships outside of Mason and Miller townships in Marion County, Missouri, are prejudiced against the applicant;

(2) That the opposite party has an undue influence over the inhabitants of Marion County, Missouri, outside of the townships of Mason and Miller.

2. When such change of venue is allowed from said district number 1 of circuit court of Marion County, Missouri, the cause shall be certified and transferred as provided by law for changes of venue from other circuit courts, and the court to which said cause is so transferred including district number 2 of the circuit court of Marion County, Missouri, shall have power and jurisdiction to dispose of the same as is provided by law in other cases of change of venue.

norms.heading: Change of venue from Marion County when people are prejudiced.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 508 Venue and Change of Venue

norms.text: Notwithstanding the provisions of sections 508.320 and 508.330, if, in any civil or criminal case pending in districts 1 or 2 of the circuit court of Marion County, the application for change of venue alleges that the inhabitants of Marion County are prejudiced against the applicant, or that the opposite party has an undue influence over the inhabitants of Marion County, then such change of venue may be awarded to any circuit court, outside of Marion county, in the same, adjoining or next adjoining circuit where the causes complained of do not exist, and the court to which said cause is so transferred shall have power and jurisdiction to dispose of the same as is provided by law in other cases of change of venue.

norms.heading: Shall be petition and answer — reply if answer contains counterclaim.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings
