norms.text: There shall be a petition and an answer; and there shall be a reply if the answer contains a counterclaim denominated as such; an answer to a cross-claim, if the answer contains a cross-claim; a third-party petition if leave is given to summon a person who was not an original party; and there shall be a third-party answer, if a third-party petition is served. No other pleading shall be required except that the court may order a reply to an answer or a third-party answer.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article soumet les demandes relatives au prénom à la procédure écrite ordinaire et limite l’exécution provisoire aux cas où le juge l’ordonne. La Rule 95.01 encadre la pétition de changement de nom, tandis que les RSMo 506.110 et 509.010 traitent respectivement de l’introduction par pétition et des actes de procédure; aucun ne reprend expressément la règle d’exécution provisoire.
correspondences.note_en: The article subjects given-name applications to ordinary written procedure and makes provisional enforcement available only when ordered. Rule 95.01 governs the contents of a name-change petition, while RSMo 506.110 and 509.010 address commencement by petition and pleadings; none expressly reproduces the provisional-enforcement rule.

norms.heading: Caption of pleading — what set forth.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: Every pleading shall contain a caption setting forth the name of the court, the title of the action, the file number, and a designation as in section 509.010. In the petition the title of the action shall include the names of all the parties, but in other pleadings it is sufficient to state the name of the first party on each side with an appropriate indication of other parties.

norms.heading: Pleading attributed to, by whom — declaration.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: Every pleading of a party represented by an attorney shall be attributed to at least one attorney of record in his individual name, whose address shall be stated. A party who is not represented by an attorney shall affix his name to his pleading and state his address. Except when otherwise specifically provided by rule or statute, pleadings need not be verified or accompanied by affidavit. Pleadings shall be attributed to a party or attorney or signed in the manner provided by supreme court rule. Any statutory requirement that pleadings be signed by any person shall be satisfied by compliance with such rules. Any statutory requirement that pleadings be acknowledged under oath, verified or notarized may be satisfied by a declaration that the pleading is made under penalty of perjury.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 808 impose que la demande soit formée par un avocat ou, dans certains cas, par un officier public ou ministériel. Les textes du Missouri exigent l’attribution ou la signature d’un avocat pour les actes représentés, mais admettent aussi l’autoreprésentation et ne prévoient pas la même catégorie d’officiers.
correspondences.note_en: Article 808 requires the application to be made by an attorney or, in specified cases, by a public or ministerial officer. The Missouri provisions require attribution or signature by counsel for represented filings but also permit self-representation and do not establish the same officer category.

correspondences.note_fr: Les observations des parties, lorsque la représentation est obligatoire, doivent être signées par un avocat aux Conseils. Les textes du Missouri imposent une signature ou attribution à un avocat de référence, mais ne prévoient pas la qualification spéciale d’avocat aux Conseils.
correspondences.note_en: Where representation is mandatory, party observations must be signed by an avocat aux Conseils. Missouri requires motions and pleadings to be signed or attributed to an attorney of record, but does not impose the French specialized-qualification requirement.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article énumère des mentions obligatoires et exige la date ainsi que les signatures des deux époux et de leur avocat. RSMo 452.310 impose la vérification et certaines mentions ; RSMo 452.312 impose des identifiants et renseignements sur les employeurs ; Rule 55.03 et RSMo 509.030 régissent la signature et les déclarations.
correspondences.note_en: The article specifies mandatory contents and requires dating and signatures by both spouses and their lawyer. RSMo 452.310 requires verification and specified information; RSMo 452.312 requires identifying and employer information; Rule 55.03 and RSMo 509.030 govern signatures and declarations.

norms.heading: Technical forms not required in pleading.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: Each averment of a pleading shall be simple, concise, and direct. No technical forms of pleading or motions are required.

norms.heading: Pleading, setting forth claim for relief, contents — demand for dollar amount not permitted, exception — discovery used to determine total damages, use in trial prohibited.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text:
1. A pleading which sets forth a claim for relief, whether an original claim, counterclaim, crossclaim or third-party claim shall contain:

(1) A short and plain statement of the facts showing that the pleader is entitled to relief; and

(2) A demand for judgment for the relief to which he deems himself entitled. The prayer for relief need not include a request for prejudgment interest otherwise properly allowable under subsection 2 of section 408.040.

If a recovery of money be demanded, no dollar amount or figure shall be included in the demand except to determine the proper jurisdictional authority, but the prayer shall be for such damages as are fair and reasonable. The provisions of this section shall not affect the conduct of trial with regard to stating, proving, or arguing damages. Relief in the alternative or of several different types may be demanded.

2. A party may discover the total damages being claimed. The response to such discovery shall not be used at trial by opposing parties for any purpose.
revisor_notes: Medical and health care providers, malpractice sections, Chap. 538; 509.050 not applicable, 538.300

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 6 impose aux parties d’alléguer les faits propres à fonder leurs prétentions. Les règles Missouri exigent l’exposé des faits fondant une demande ou une défense, mais ne formulent pas exactement une charge générale d’allégation.
correspondences.note_en: Article 6 places on parties the burden of alleging facts supporting their claims. The Missouri provisions require factual statements supporting claims or defenses, but do not state the same general burden in identical terms.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1360 impose, à peine d’irrecevabilité, la description sommaire du patrimoine, les intentions de répartition et les diligences amiables. La Rule 96.05 exige certaines mentions dans une requête en partage, tandis que RSMo 509.050 énonce seulement les exigences générales des demandes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1360 requires, on pain of inadmissibility, a summary description of the assets, the claimant’s proposed allocation, and efforts toward an amicable partition. Rule 96.05 requires specified contents in a partition petition, while RSMo 509.050 states only general pleading requirements.

norms.heading: Joinder of claims.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: The plaintiff in his petition or in a reply setting forth a counterclaim and the defendant in an answer setting forth a counterclaim may join either as independent or as alternate claims as many claims either legal or equitable or both as he may have against an opposing party. There may be a like joinder of claims where there are multiple parties if the requirements of sections 507.030, 507.040 and 507.060 are satisfied. There may be a like joinder of cross-claims or third-party claims if the requirements of section 509.460 and section 507.080, respectively, are satisfied.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article règle l’incidence, sur la compétence et le taux du ressort, du regroupement de prétentions distinctes ou connexes. Le Missouri autorise la jonction de plusieurs demandes (RSMo 509.060; Rule 55.06), tandis que le § 517.081 traite seulement du dépassement de compétence résultant notamment d’une consolidation.
correspondences.note_en: The article determines the effect of joining distinct or related claims on jurisdiction and appealability. Missouri permits joinder of multiple claims (RSMo 509.060; Rule 55.06), while § 517.081 addresses only jurisdictional excess resulting, among other things, from consolidation.

frcp.evidence: s prior Rules 55.07 and 55.08. Paragraph (a) is the same as Rule 18(a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.heading: Two claims may be joined in a single action, when — court shall grant relief, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: Whenever a claim is one heretofore cognizable only after another claim has been prosecuted to a conclusion, the two claims may be joined in a single action; but the court shall grant relief in that action only in accordance with the relative substantive rights of the parties. In particular, a plaintiff may state a claim for money and a claim to have set aside a conveyance fraudulent as to him, without first having obtained a judgment establishing the claim for money; a plaintiff may state his original claim against the defendant and also in either the original or an amended petition or a reply, a claim for having any release, composition, settlement, or discharge of the original claim set aside as fraudulent or otherwise wrongfully procured.

norms.heading: Defenses — form of denials.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: A party shall state in short and plain terms his defenses to each claim asserted and shall admit or deny the averments upon which the adverse party relies. If he is without knowledge or information sufficient to form a belief as to the truth of an averment, he shall so state and this has the effect of a denial. Denials shall fairly meet the substance of the averments denied. When a pleader intends in good faith to deny only a part or a qualification of an averment, he shall specify so much of it as is true and material and shall deny only the remainder. Unless the pleader intends in good faith to controvert all the averments of the preceding pleading, he may make his denials as specific denials of designated averments or paragraphs, or he may generally deny all the averments except such designated averments or paragraphs as he expressly admits; but, when he does so intend to controvert all its averments he may do so by general denial.

norms.heading: Affirmative defenses.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: In pleading to a preceding pleading, a party shall set forth affirmatively accord and satisfaction, arbitration and award, assumption of risk, contributory negligence, discharge in bankruptcy, duress, estoppel, failure of consideration, fraud, illegality, injury by fellow servant, laches, license, payment, release, res judicata, statute of frauds, statute of limitations, truth in defamation, waiver, and any other matter constituting an avoidance or affirmative defense. When a party has mistakenly designated a defense as a counterclaim or a counterclaim as a defense, the court shall treat the pleadings as if there had been a proper designation.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 617 concerne la contrariété de jugements après l’échec d’une fin de non-recevoir fondée sur l’autorité de la chose jugée. Les Rule 55.08 et RSMo 509.090 imposent de soulever la res judicata comme défense affirmative, sans organiser le recours pour contrariété.
correspondences.note_en: Article 617 concerns conflicting judgments after an unsuccessful res judicata objection. Rule 55.08 and RSMo 509.090 require res judicata to be pleaded as an affirmative defense, but do not provide the conflicting-judgments remedy.

norms.heading: Failure to deny, effect.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: Averments in a pleading to which a responsive pleading is required, other than those as to the amount of damage, are admitted when not denied in the responsive pleadings. When a reply is filed, whether required or not, all affirmative defenses of the answer which are not denied in the reply are deemed admitted. Averments in a pleading to which a responsive pleading is not filed and is not required shall be taken as denied or avoided.

norms.heading: Pleading in alternative — consistency.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: A party may set forth two or more statements of a claim or defense alternately or hypothetically, either in one count or defense or in separate counts or defenses. When two or more statements are made in the alternative and one of them if made independently would be sufficient, the pleading is not made insufficient by the insufficiency of one or more of the alternative statements. A party may also state as many separate claims or defenses as he has whether based on legal or on equitable grounds or on both.

norms.heading: Averments, how made.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: All averments of claim or defense shall be made in numbered paragraphs, the contents of each of which shall be limited as far as practicable to a statement of a single set of circumstances; and a paragraph may be referred to by number in all succeeding pleadings. Each claim founded upon a separate transaction or occurrence and each defense other than denials shall be stated in a separate count or defense whenever a separation facilitates the clear presentation of the matters set forth.

norms.heading: Adoption of statements by reference — exhibits.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: Statements in a pleading may be adopted by reference in a different part of the same pleading or in another pleading or in any motion. An exhibit to a pleading is a part thereof for all purposes.

norms.heading: Averments as to capacity or authority of parties to sue or be sued.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: It shall be sufficient to aver the ultimate fact of the capacity of a party to sue or be sued or the authority of a party to sue or be sued in a representative capacity or the legal existence of a corporation or of an organized association of persons that is made a party. When a person desires to raise an issue as to the legal existence of any party or the capacity of any party to sue or be sued or the authority of a party to sue or be sued in a representative capacity, he shall do so by specific negative averment, which shall include such supporting particulars as are peculiarly within the pleader's knowledge. When a party so raises such issue, the burden of proof thereon shall be placed upon the opposite party.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 9 met à la charge de chaque partie la preuve des faits nécessaires au succès de sa prétention. Les textes du Missouri imposent surtout un soutien probatoire des allégations et prévoient une charge de la preuve pour certaines questions ou actions particulières, sans énoncer une règle générale identique.
correspondences.note_en: Article 9 places on each party the burden of proving facts necessary to prevail. The Missouri provisions chiefly require evidentiary support for factual contentions and allocate the burden for particular issues or proceedings, but do not state the same general rule.

norms.heading: Partnership deemed confessed, unless denied.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: When parties sue or are sued as a partnership, and the names of the partners are set forth in the petition or counterclaim, the existence of the partnership shall be deemed confessed unless it be denied by specific negative averment, which shall include such supporting particulars as are peculiarly within the pleader's knowledge.

norms.heading: Particularity required in all averments of fraud or mistake.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: In all averments of fraud or mistake, the circumstances constituting fraud or mistake shall be stated with particularity. Malice, intent, knowledge, and other condition of mind of a person may be averred generally.

norms.heading: Conditions precedent — how pleaded.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: In pleading the performance or occurrence of conditions precedent, it is sufficient to aver generally that all conditions precedent have been performed or have occurred. A denial of performance or occurrence shall be made specifically and with particularity, and when so made, the party pleading the performance or occurrence shall establish on the trial the facts showing such performance or occurrence.

norms.heading: Official documents or acts, form of pleading.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: In pleading an official document or official act it is sufficient to aver that the document was issued or the act done in compliance with law.

norms.heading: Judgments and decisions, form of pleading.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: In pleading a judgment or decision of a domestic or foreign court, judicial or quasi-judicial tribunal, or of a board or officer, it is sufficient to aver the judgment or decision without setting forth matter showing jurisdiction to render it. If such allegations be controverted, the party pleading them shall establish on the trial the facts conferring jurisdiction.

norms.heading: Claims of items of special damage shall be specifically stated.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: When items of special damage are claimed, they shall be specifically stated. In actions where exemplary or punitive damages are recoverable, the petition shall state separately the amount of such damages sought to be recovered.

norms.heading: Libel and slander, averments — defenses.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: In an action for libel or slander, it shall not be necessary to state in the petition any extrinsic facts, for the purpose of showing the application to the plaintiff of the defamatory matter out of which the claim arose, but it shall be sufficient to state, generally, that the same was published or spoken concerning the plaintiff; and if such allegation be not controverted in the answer, it shall not be necessary to prove it on the trial; in other cases it shall be necessary. The defendant may, in his answer, allege both the truth of the matter charged as defamatory and any mitigating circumstances admissible in evidence to reduce the amount of damages; and whether he prove the justification or not, he may give in evidence the mitigating circumstance.

norms.heading: Private statutes, averments — laws of other states — judicial notice.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text:
1. In pleading a private statute or a right derived therefrom, it shall be sufficient to refer to such statute by its title and the place where found in the session acts or in the revised statutes, and the court shall thereupon take judicial notice thereof.

2. In every action or proceeding wherein the pleading states that the law of another state is relied upon, the courts of this state shall take judicial notice of the public statutes and judicial decisions of said state.

norms.heading: Pleading written instrument.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: Whenever a claim, defense, or counterclaim is founded upon a written instrument, the same may be pleaded according to legal effect, or may be recited at length in the pleading, or a copy may be attached to the pleading as an exhibit.

norms.heading: Execution of written instrument deemed confessed, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: When any claim or counterclaim shall be founded upon any written instrument and the same shall be set up at length in the pleading or a copy attached thereto as an exhibit, the execution of such instrument shall be deemed confessed unless the party charged to have executed the same shall specifically deny the execution thereof.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 300 impose que l’assignation expose les moyens de faux et somme le défendeur de déclarer s’il entend utiliser l’écrit. La Rule 55.22 exige la reproduction ou la production de l’instrument, tandis que le RSMo 509.240 prévoit le déni spécifique de son exécution, sans organiser la sommation relative à son usage.
correspondences.note_en: Article 300 requires the summons to state the grounds of forgery and demand that the defendant declare whether he will use the writing. Rule 55.22 requires the instrument to be pleaded or attached, while RSMo 509.240 requires a specific denial of execution but does not provide the use-declaration procedure.

norms.heading: Pleadings, how construed.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: All pleadings shall be so construed as to do substantial justice.

norms.heading: Time of pleading.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text:
1. A defendant shall file his answer within thirty days after the service of the summons and petition upon him, except where service by mail is had, in which event a defendant shall file his answer within thirty days after the return registered mail receipt, as required by subsection 2 of section 506.160 and subsection 3 of section 506.180, is filed in the case, or within forty-five days after the first publication of notice in case that neither personal service nor service by mail is had.

2. If a cross-claim be filed against a party, he shall file an answer thereto within twenty days after the same be filed. The plaintiff shall file his reply to a counterclaim in the answer within twenty days after filing of the answer or, if a reply is ordered by the court, within twenty days after entry of the order, unless the order otherwise directs.

3. The filing of any motion provided for in sections 509.290 to 509.320 alters the time fixed for filing any required responsive pleadings as follows, unless a different time is fixed by order of the court: If the court denies the motion or postpones its disposition until the trial on the merits, the responsive pleading may be filed within ten days after notice of the court's action; if the court grants a motion for a more definite statement or for a bill of particulars, the responsive pleading may be filed within ten days after the filing of the more definite statement or bill of particulars. In either case the time for filing of the responsive pleading shall be no less than remains of the time which would have been allowed under this section if the motion had not been made.

norms.heading: Demurrers and pleas in abatement and to the jurisdiction shall not be used.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: Demurrers and pleas in abatement and to the jurisdiction shall not be used.

norms.heading: Motions, form of.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text:
1. An application to the court for an order shall be by motion which, unless made during a hearing or trial, shall be made in writing, shall state with particularity the grounds therefor, and shall set forth the relief or order sought. The requirement of writing is fulfilled if the motion is stated in a written notice of the hearing of the motion.

2. The provisions applicable to captions, signing, and other matters of form of pleadings apply to all motions and other papers provided for by this code.

norms.heading: Objections which may be raised by motions.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 49 permet à la juridiction compétente de connaître des moyens de défense, sauf compétence exclusive d’une autre juridiction, et prévoit le renvoi d’une question administrative préjudicielle sérieuse. Rule 55.27 et RSMo 509.290 organisent plusieurs défenses et objections de compétence, mais ne prévoient pas ce mécanisme complet de question préjudicielle administrative.
correspondences.note_en: Article 49 allows the court with jurisdiction to hear all defenses, except matters within another court’s exclusive jurisdiction, and requires referral and a stay for a serious administrative preliminary question. Rule 55.27 and RSMo 509.290 address several jurisdictional defenses and objections, but not the full administrative referral mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 75 impose que l'exception d'incompétence soit motivée et indique la juridiction demandée. La Rule 55.26 exige une motivation précise et le dispositif sollicité ; la Rule 51.045 impose, en matière de venue, d'indiquer les comtés et le fondement, mais ces textes ne couvrent pas exactement toute l'incompétence française.
correspondences.note_en: Article 75 requires the jurisdictional objection to state its grounds and identify the requested court. Rule 55.26 requires particular grounds and the relief sought; Rule 51.045 requires identifying proper counties and their basis for improper venue, but neither fully covers French jurisdictional objections.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 77 autorise, dans certains cas, le relevé d'office de l'incompétence territoriale. La Rule 51.045 organise la demande de transfert pour improper venue, avec un délai et une renonciation ; RSMo 509.290 permet de soulever l'improper venue par motion ; RSMo 508.010 prévoit le transfert depuis un comté inapproprié, sans reprendre les distinctions françaises.
correspondences.note_en: Article 77 permits sua sponte territorial-jurisdiction review in specified proceedings. Rule 51.045 governs a motion to transfer for improper venue, including a deadline and waiver; RSMo 509.290 permits improper venue to be raised by motion; RSMo 508.010 provides transfer from an improper county without reproducing the French distinctions.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 100 impose, en cas de litige identique pendant devant deux juridictions de même degré également compétentes, le dessaisissement de la juridiction saisie en second, sur demande, ou d'office. Les textes du Missouri permettent d'opposer l'existence d'une autre action identique, mais sans reprendre exactement la règle du second saisi; l'article 452.765 vise spécialement la garde des enfants.
correspondences.note_en: Article 100 requires the second court to decline jurisdiction when the same dispute is pending before two equally competent courts of the same level, on request or sua sponte. Missouri permits a motion based on another action involving the same parties and cause, but does not reproduce the same second-filed rule; RSMo 452.765 is specific to child-custody proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 120 impose, pour certaines nullités de fond d’ordre public, un relevé d’office, et permet celui du défaut de capacité d’ester en justice. Rule 55.27 et RSMo 509.290 permettent d’invoquer l’incapacité par motion, mais ne prévoient pas le même relevé d’office ni le régime général des nullités d’actes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 120 requires certain public-order substantive nullities to be raised ex officio and permits the court to raise lack of legal capacity to sue ex officio. Rule 55.27 and RSMo 509.290 allow capacity objections by motion, but do not provide the same ex-officio rule or a general regime for nullities of procedural acts.

correspondences.note_fr: Les textes du Missouri organisent diverses objections et prévoient le rejet d’office en cas d’absence de compétence matérielle. Ils ne couvrent pas expressément la chose jugée, les délais ou l’absence d’ouverture d’une voie de recours, ni le traitement conjoint d’une question de fond et de la fin de non-recevoir.
correspondences.note_en: The Missouri texts govern various objections and require sua sponte dismissal for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction. They do not expressly cover res judicata, appellate deadlines or unavailable appellate remedies, nor the joint disposition of a preliminary merits issue and the procedural bar.

norms.heading: Failure to state a claim or defense, raised on motion, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: The objections of failure to state a claim upon which relief can be granted or to state a legal defense to a claim may be raised by motion when these objections appear on the face of the pleadings.

norms.heading: Motion for more definite statement or for a bill of particulars.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: A party may move for a more definite statement or for a bill of particulars of any matter contained in a petition, answer or reply which is not averred with sufficient definiteness or particularity to enable him properly to prepare his responsive pleadings or to prepare generally for trial when a responsive pleading is not required. If the motion is granted and the order of the court is not obeyed within ten days after notice of the order, or within such other time as the court may fix, the court may strike the pleading to which the motion was directed, or make such order as it deems just. A bill of particulars becomes a part of the pleading which it supplements.

norms.heading: Matter which party may move to strike out.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: A party may move to strike any redundant, immaterial, impertinent, or scandalous matter from any pleading.

norms.heading: Time allowed for making motions.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: All motions made shall be made within the time allowed for responding to the opposing party's pleading or, if no responsive pleading is permitted, within twenty days after the service of the last pleading. Motions and pleadings may be filed simultaneously by the same party without waiver of the matters contained in either.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 74 impose la présentation simultanée et préalable des exceptions, sous peine d’irrecevabilité, et prévoit leur concentration ainsi que certaines réserves. Rule 55.27 et RSMo 509.330, 509.340 et 509.400 organisent des délais, la jonction et la renonciation, mais selon des conditions et exceptions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 74 requires procedural exceptions to be raised simultaneously and before merits defenses or pleas of inadmissibility, subject to waiver, with specified reservations. Rule 55.27 and RSMo 509.330, 509.340, and 509.400 address timing, joinder, and waiver, but with materially different conditions and exceptions.

norms.heading: Consolidation of motions — waiver of objections — exceptions.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: A party who makes a motion may join with it the other motions provided for and then available to him. No objection is waived by being joined with one or more other objections in the motion, nor shall pleading over or entering into the trial of the merits be deemed to waive any objection properly raised by motion. A party waives all objections and other matters then available to him by motion by failure to assert the same by motion within the time limited by section 509.330, except failure to state a claim upon which relief can be granted, or failure to state a legal defense to a claim, and except lack of jurisdiction over the subject matter.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 74 impose la présentation simultanée et préalable des exceptions, sous peine d’irrecevabilité, et prévoit leur concentration ainsi que certaines réserves. Rule 55.27 et RSMo 509.330, 509.340 et 509.400 organisent des délais, la jonction et la renonciation, mais selon des conditions et exceptions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 74 requires procedural exceptions to be raised simultaneously and before merits defenses or pleas of inadmissibility, subject to waiver, with specified reservations. Rule 55.27 and RSMo 509.330, 509.340, and 509.400 address timing, joinder, and waiver, but with materially different conditions and exceptions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 103 permet de soulever la connexité à tout moment, sauf tardiveté dilatoire. La Rule 55.27(a)(9) prévoit une exception pour une autre action pendante entre les mêmes parties et pour la même cause, tandis que la RSMo 509.340 encadre la réunion des motions et la renonciation aux objections dans les délais; ces règles sont plus étroites.
correspondences.note_en: Article 103 permits a connexity exception at any time unless raised late for dilatory purposes. Rule 55.27(a)(9) addresses another pending action between the same parties for the same cause, while RSMo 509.340 governs joining motions and waiver of objections within the applicable time limits; these provisions are narrower.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 111 permet au bénéficiaire d’un délai pour faire inventaire et délibérer de différer la présentation de ses autres exceptions jusqu’à l’expiration de ce délai. Les Rule 55.27 et RSMo 509.340 organisent la présentation, la jonction et la renonciation aux moyens, mais ne prévoient pas ce délai successoral spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: Article 111 allows a person benefiting from a period to inventory and deliberate to postpone asserting other procedural exceptions until that period expires. Rule 55.27 and RSMo 509.340 regulate the assertion, joinder, and waiver of defenses or objections, but do not provide this specific succession-related postponement.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 112 permet d’invoquer la nullité au fur et à mesure, mais la couvre si celui qui l’invoque soulève ensuite une défense au fond ou une fin de non-recevoir. Les textes du Missouri prévoient aussi des mécanismes de renonciation ou de forclusion des objections, mais selon des conditions différentes, notamment l’omission d’une motion ou d’une réponse.
correspondences.note_en: Article 112 permits procedural nullity to be raised as the act occurs but deems it waived if the party invoking it later pleads to the merits or raises a non-receivability defense. Missouri likewise provides waiver mechanisms for omitted objections, but under materially different conditions, especially omission from a motion or responsive pleading.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 113 impose que tous les moyens de nullité concernant des actes déjà accomplis soient soulevés simultanément, sous peine d’irrecevabilité ultérieure. La Rule 55.27 et le RSMo 509.340 imposent également la concentration des objections disponibles, mais leur champ et leurs modalités diffèrent.
correspondences.note_en: Article 113 requires all available nullity grounds concerning completed procedural acts to be raised simultaneously, or later grounds are inadmissible. Rule 55.27 and RSMo 509.340 similarly require consolidation of available objections, but their scope and mechanics differ.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet de soulever l’exception de nullité en tout état de cause, sous réserve d’une sanction pour manœuvre dilatoire. Les dispositions du Missouri encadrent au contraire les délais et prévoient la déchéance de certaines objections non soulevées à temps, avec des exceptions limitées.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits a substantive nullity objection at any stage, subject to possible damages for dilatory conduct. Missouri provisions instead impose timing requirements and waiver for certain objections not timely raised, with limited exceptions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise en principe les fins de non-recevoir à tout moment, sous réserve de règles contraires, et permet des dommages-intérêts en cas de retard dilatoire. La Rule 55.27 et RSMo 509.340 organisent plutôt des délais et la renonciation à certains moyens; la Rule 55.03 prévoit des sanctions pour conduite destinée à retarder la procédure.
correspondences.note_en: The article generally permits procedural bars at any stage, subject to contrary rules, while allowing damages for dilatory delay. Rule 55.27 and RSMo 509.340 instead establish motion deadlines and waiver, while Rule 55.03 provides sanctions for conduct intended to cause unnecessary delay.

correspondences.note_fr: Les textes du Missouri organisent diverses objections et prévoient le rejet d’office en cas d’absence de compétence matérielle. Ils ne couvrent pas expressément la chose jugée, les délais ou l’absence d’ouverture d’une voie de recours, ni le traitement conjoint d’une question de fond et de la fin de non-recevoir.
correspondences.note_en: The Missouri texts govern various objections and require sua sponte dismissal for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction. They do not expressly cover res judicata, appellate deadlines or unavailable appellate remedies, nor the joint disposition of a preliminary merits issue and the procedural bar.

correspondences.note_fr: La conclusion de la convention interrompt, sous condition, le délai de péremption de l'instance, sans dessaisir le juge, qui conserve compétence pour les incidents, exceptions, fins de non-recevoir et mesures provisoires. Les textes du Missouri couvrent certaines défenses et objections procédurales, leur présentation et la continuation de l'instance, mais non l'interruption conventionnelle de la péremption ni l'ensemble de ces effets.
correspondences.note_en: The agreement conditionally interrupts the procedural expiration period while preserving the judge’s authority over procedural incidents, objections, defenses, and provisional measures. Missouri addresses some procedural defenses and objections, their presentation, and continuances, but not convention-based interruption of the expiration period or all of these effects.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article encadre la nullité liée à la composition irrégulière de la juridiction et impose une contestation immédiate, sous peine de forclusion. Les textes du Missouri prévoient plus généralement la renonciation aux objections non soulevées par motion ou dans les écritures, sans régler spécifiquement la composition de la juridiction.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs nullity based on an irregularly constituted court and requires an immediate objection, failing which the objection is waived. The Missouri provisions establish more general waiver rules for objections omitted from a motion or responsive pleading, without specifically addressing court composition.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article attribue une compétence exclusive au tribunal judiciaire pour les contestations de nationalité et prévoit que l’exception d’incompétence est d’ordre public, invocable en tout état de cause et relevée d’office. Le RSMo 509.340 prévoit seulement que le défaut de compétence matérielle n’est pas couvert par la renonciation aux exceptions.
correspondences.note_en: The article assigns exclusive jurisdiction over nationality disputes and makes subject-matter jurisdiction objections public-order matters that may be raised at any time and sua sponte. RSMo 509.340 only provides that lack of subject-matter jurisdiction is not waived.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit la renonciation à invoquer tardivement une irrégularité connue. La Rule 57.07 prévoit une renonciation pour certaines irrégularités de déposition, tandis que les RSMo 509.340 et 509.400 organisent plus généralement la perte de certaines objections non soulevées en temps utile, avec des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article waives a known procedural irregularity when not raised timely. Rule 57.07 applies this principle to deposition irregularities, while RSMo 509.340 and 509.400 address waiver of objections more generally, under materially different conditions.

norms.heading: Motion searches record.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: Upon motion directed to an answer or reply, substantial defects in all prior pleadings may be considered and judgment rendered against the party who has first failed to state a claim upon which relief can be granted or to state a legal defense to a claim.

norms.heading: Motion for judgment on pleadings.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: After the pleadings are closed, but within such time as not to delay the trial, any party may move for judgment on the pleadings.

norms.heading: Time for hearing of motions.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: All objections raised by motion shall be heard and determined before the trial on application of any party, unless the court for good cause orders that the hearing and determination thereof be deferred until the trial.

norms.heading: Place of hearing.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: All motions may be heard and other acts or proceedings, except trials upon the merits, may be done or conducted by a judge in chambers, without the attendance of the clerk or other court officials and at any place either within or without the county; but no hearing, other than one ex parte, shall be conducted outside the county without the consent of all parties affected thereby.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit que les mesures d’instruction devant la juridiction se déroulent en audience publique ou en chambre du conseil. La Rule 55.29 et le RSMo 509.380 autorisent certains actes en chambre, mais aucun des deux textes ne reproduit expressément ce régime pour les mesures d’instruction.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires evidentiary measures conducted before the court to take place in open court or in chambers. Rule 55.29 and RSMo 509.380 permit certain acts in chambers, but neither expressly establishes this regime for evidentiary measures.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet au juge de se déplacer pour exécuter ou surveiller une mesure sans l’assistance du greffier. La Rule 55.29 et le RSMo 509.380 autorisent certains actes du juge en chambre sans présence du greffier, mais prévoient des restrictions territoriales et d’audience.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits a judge to travel to conduct or attend an evidentiary measure without the clerk. Rule 55.29 and RSMo 509.380 allow certain judicial acts in chambers without the clerk’s attendance, but impose territorial and hearing-related restrictions.

correspondences.note_fr: Si la vérification n'est pas immédiate, le juge en fixe le lieu, le jour et l'heure, et peut désigner un membre de la formation. Les règles du Missouri traitent du lieu des actes judiciaires et imposent que les ordonnances d'examen précisent notamment le temps et le lieu, sans prévoir cette désignation.
correspondences.note_en: If verification is not immediate, the judge sets its place, date, and time and may designate a member of the panel. Missouri rules address the place of judicial acts and require examination orders to specify time and place, but do not provide the same designation mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 231 permet au juge d’entendre immédiatement des tiers, à l’audience, en cabinet ou sur le lieu d’exécution d’une mesure d’instruction. La Rule 55.29 et le RSMo 509.380 autorisent les actes du juge en cabinet et en tout lieu, mais ne prévoient pas spécifiquement cette audition immédiate et imposent des limites territoriales aux audiences.
correspondences.note_en: Article 231 permits the judge to hear third parties immediately, at the hearing, in chambers, or wherever an investigative measure is being carried out. Rule 55.29 and RSMo 509.380 allow judicial proceedings in chambers and at any place, but do not specifically provide for this immediate hearing and impose territorial limits on hearings.

correspondences.note_fr: En matière gracieuse, l’examen doit avoir lieu en chambre du conseil. Les règles du Missouri autorisent les actes et procédures autres que les procès au fond à être conduits en chambre, mais ne désignent pas spécifiquement la matière gracieuse ni ne rendent cette modalité obligatoire.
correspondences.note_en: In non-contentious matters, the application must be heard in chambers. Missouri permits proceedings other than trials on the merits to occur in chambers, but does not specifically identify non-contentious matters or make that procedure mandatory.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la procédure écrite ordinaire, l’instruction en chambre du conseil après avis du ministère public et le prononcé public. Les textes du Missouri prévoient que les actes autres que le procès au fond peuvent se tenir en chambre, mais ne règlent ni l’avis du ministère public ni le prononcé public.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires ordinary written procedure, chamber proceedings after the public prosecutor’s opinion, and judgment pronounced publicly. The Missouri provisions allow proceedings other than trials on the merits to occur in chambers, but address neither prosecutorial input nor public pronouncement.

correspondences.note_fr: L’affaire est instruite et jugée en chambre du conseil. Les textes du Missouri autorisent généralement les actes et procédures autres que les procès au fond à être conduits en chambre, mais exigent que les procès au fond se tiennent en audience publique.
correspondences.note_en: The matter is investigated and decided in chambers. Missouri provisions generally permit proceedings other than trials on the merits to occur in chambers, but require trials on the merits to be conducted in open court.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet au juge de tenter une conciliation selon les modalités, le lieu et le moment qu’il fixe, y compris en chambre du conseil sans greffier, et impose un procès-verbal signé. Le RSMo 509.380 couvre seulement la tenue d’actes en chambre et en l’absence du greffier; les Rules 88.03 et 88.08 concernent une médiation distincte et ne reprennent pas cette formalisation.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits the judge to attempt conciliation under terms, at a place and time of the judge’s choosing, including in chambers without the clerk, and requires a signed record of the agreement. RSMo 509.380 covers only in-chambers proceedings without the clerk; Rules 88.03 and 88.08 concern a distinct mediation process and do not replicate this record requirement.

norms.heading: Regular times and places for hearing motions.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text:
1. Unless local conditions make it impracticable, each trial court shall establish regular times and places, at intervals sufficiently frequent for the prompt dispatch of business, at which motions requiring notice and hearing may be heard and disposed of; but the court at any time or place and on such notice, if any, as he considers reasonable may make orders for the advancement, conduct, and hearing of actions.

2. To expedite its business, the court may make provision by rule or order for the submission and determination of motions without oral hearing upon brief written statements of reasons in support and opposition.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit que l’ordonnance est rendue après que les avocats ont été entendus ou appelés, avec convocation par le juge et une procédure urgente par notification entre avocats. La Rule 55.30 et le RSMo 509.390 organisent les audiences sur motions et permettent au tribunal de fixer les modalités et le préavis, mais sans ces modalités françaises précises.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides for an order after counsel have been heard or called, including judicial summons and an urgent invitation by inter-attorney notice. Rule 55.30 and RSMo 509.390 regulate motion hearings and permit the court to set notice and hearing arrangements, but do not contain these specific French procedures.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article pose le principe de l’oralité, permet aux parties de convenir d’une procédure sans audience et prévoit une procédure écrite spéciale pour la révision de la prestation compensatoire. Les textes du Missouri permettent la décision de requêtes sans débat oral, mais seulement selon une règle ou une ordonnance et sans reprendre ces conditions familiales.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes oral proceedings, permits the parties to agree to determination without a hearing, and requires ordinary written procedure for compensatory-allowance revisions. Missouri provisions permit motions to be decided without oral argument, but under court rule or order and without these family-specific conditions.

norms.heading: Defenses which may be raised by pleading — waiver.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: All defenses and objections for which there is no provision for the raising of the same by motion shall be raised in the responsive pleading if one is permitted. When no responsive pleading is required the case shall be deemed at issue. If a responsive pleading is required all defenses or objections not raised therein are waived, except failure to state a claim upon which relief can be granted, or failure to state a legal defense to a claim, and, except lack of jurisdiction over the subject matter. All issues of fact raised or deemed to be raised shall be determined at the trial.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 72 permet de proposer les défenses au fond à tout stade de la procédure. Les textes du Missouri règlent plutôt les formes, délais et effets de la présentation des défenses, avec une préclusion de certaines objections lorsqu’elles ne sont pas soulevées à temps.
correspondences.note_en: Article 72 permits merits defenses to be raised at any stage. The Missouri provisions instead regulate the form, timing, and waiver of defenses, with certain objections waived if not timely asserted.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 74 impose la présentation simultanée et préalable des exceptions, sous peine d’irrecevabilité, et prévoit leur concentration ainsi que certaines réserves. Rule 55.27 et RSMo 509.330, 509.340 et 509.400 organisent des délais, la jonction et la renonciation, mais selon des conditions et exceptions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 74 requires procedural exceptions to be raised simultaneously and before merits defenses or pleas of inadmissibility, subject to waiver, with specified reservations. Rule 55.27 and RSMo 509.330, 509.340, and 509.400 address timing, joinder, and waiver, but with materially different conditions and exceptions.

Les textes du Missouri prévoient aussi des mécanismes de renonciation ou de forclusion des objections, mais selon des conditions différentes, notamment l’omission d’une motion ou d’une réponse.
correspondences.note_en: Article 112 permits procedural nullity to be raised as the act occurs but deems it waived if the party invoking it later pleads to the merits or raises a non-receivability defense. Missouri likewise provides waiver mechanisms for omitted objections, but under materially different conditions, especially omission from a motion or responsive pleading.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet de soulever l’exception de nullité en tout état de cause, sous réserve d’une sanction pour manœuvre dilatoire. Les dispositions du Missouri encadrent au contraire les délais et prévoient la déchéance de certaines objections non soulevées à temps, avec des exceptions limitées.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits a substantive nullity objection at any stage, subject to possible damages for dilatory conduct. Missouri provisions instead impose timing requirements and waiver for certain objections not timely raised, with limited exceptions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article encadre la nullité liée à la composition irrégulière de la juridiction et impose une contestation immédiate, sous peine de forclusion. Les textes du Missouri prévoient plus généralement la renonciation aux objections non soulevées par motion ou dans les écritures, sans régler spécifiquement la composition de la juridiction.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs nullity based on an irregularly constituted court and requires an immediate objection, failing which the objection is waived. The Missouri provisions establish more general waiver rules for objections omitted from a motion or responsive pleading, without specifically addressing court composition.

correspondences.note_fr: Le tribunal statue sur la demande, les demandes incidentes et les défenses au fond, et renvoie l'affaire en cas d'incompétence. La Rule 55.27 et le RSMo 509.400 organisent les défenses, notamment l'exception de compétence, tandis que la Rule 67.03 prévoit le rejet pour défaut de compétence, sans règle équivalente de renvoi.
correspondences.note_en: The court decides the claim, incidental claims, and defenses, and remands the case when it lacks jurisdiction. Rule 55.27 and RSMo 509.400 govern defenses, including jurisdictional objections, while Rule 67.03 provides dismissal for lack of jurisdiction rather than an equivalent remand mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Le tribunal statue sur la demande de recouvrement ainsi que sur les demandes incidentes et les défenses, avec renvoi en cas d’incompétence. Les règles du Missouri organisent la jonction des demandes, les demandes reconventionnelles et les défenses d’incompétence, mais aucun texte fourni ne prévoit le renvoi correspondant à l’article 82.
correspondences.note_en: The court adjudicates the collection claim, related claims, and defenses, with referral upon a finding of lack of jurisdiction. Missouri rules address joinder, counterclaims, and jurisdictional defenses, but none of the supplied texts provides the corresponding referral mechanism under article 82.

frcp.evidence: s prior Rules 55.07 and 55.08. Paragraph (a) is the same as Rule 18(a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure
mmittee Note – 1974 This rule is substantially the same as Rule 13 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit la renonciation à invoquer tardivement une irrégularité connue. La Rule 57.07 prévoit une renonciation pour certaines irrégularités de déposition, tandis que les RSMo 509.340 et 509.400 organisent plus généralement la perte de certaines objections non soulevées en temps utile, avec des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article waives a known procedural irregularity when not raised timely. Rule 57.07 applies this principle to deposition irregularities, while RSMo 509.340 and 509.400 address waiver of objections more generally, under materially different conditions.

norms.heading: Objection that no demand has been made not available, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: It shall not hereafter be available to a party as an objection that no demand for the subject matter of a suit was made prior to its institution, unless it is expressly set up by way of defense in the answer or replication, and is also accompanied with a tender of the amount that is due; in which case, if the plaintiff will further prosecute his suit, and shall not recover a greater sum than is tendered, he shall pay all costs. This provision shall be applicable as well to actions for property as for money; when property is tendered the damages for its detention, if any, shall also be tendered.

norms.heading: What a pleading shall state as a counterclaim.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: A pleading shall state as a counterclaim any claim, not the subject of a pending action, which at the time of filing the pleading the pleader has against any opposing party, if it arises out of the transaction or occurrences that is the subject matter of the opposing party's claim and does not require for its adjudication the presence of third parties of whom the court cannot acquire jurisdiction.

norms.heading: Counterclaim exceeding opposing claim.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: A counterclaim may or may not diminish or defeat the recovery sought by the opposing party. It may claim relief exceeding in amount or different in kind from that sought in the pleading of the opposing party.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 37 permet au juge saisi selon le montant de connaître de certaines demandes incidentes et reconventionnelles inférieures à son taux, même si leur réunion dépasse ce taux. Les textes du Missouri autorisent les demandes reconventionnelles supérieures à la demande adverse, mais ne prévoient ni cette règle d’agrégation ni une procédure de certification.
correspondences.note_en: Article 37 allows the court to hear certain smaller incidental and counterclaims despite their aggregate exceeding its jurisdictional threshold. The Missouri texts regulate counterclaims exceeding the opposing claim, but do not state that aggregate-amount rule or any certification procedure.

frcp.evidence: mmittee Note – 1974 This rule is substantially the same as Rule 13 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 38 prévoit, lorsqu’une demande incidente dépasse le taux de compétence, soit une décision limitée à la demande initiale, soit le renvoi de l’ensemble, ainsi qu’une exception pour certaines demandes reconventionnelles en dommages-intérêts. Les textes du Missouri autorisent seulement une demande reconventionnelle supérieure à la demande adverse, sans ces choix ni cette exception.
correspondences.note_en: Article 38 provides alternatives when an incidental claim exceeds jurisdiction and an exception for damages counterclaims based exclusively on the original claim. The Missouri texts only permit counterclaims exceeding the opposing claim; they do not provide those alternatives or exception.

frcp.evidence: mmittee Note – 1974 This rule is substantially the same as Rule 13 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article définit la demande reconventionnelle comme une demande du défendeur visant un avantage autre que le simple rejet. La Rule 55.32(c) et le RSMo 509.430 prévoient qu’une demande reconventionnelle peut dépasser ou différer de la demande adverse et ne pas seulement la réduire ou la combattre.
correspondences.note_en: The article defines a counterclaim as a defendant’s claim seeking relief beyond simple dismissal. Rule 55.32(c) and RSMo 509.430 likewise provide that a counterclaim may exceed the opposing claim or seek relief of a different kind, rather than merely defeat it.

frcp.evidence: mmittee Note – 1974 This rule is substantially the same as Rule 13 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.heading: When claim may be presented as counterclaim by supplemental pleading.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: A claim which either matured or was acquired by the pleader after serving his pleading may, with the permission of the court, be presented as a counterclaim by supplemental pleading.

norms.heading: Counterclaim set up by amendment, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: When a pleader fails to set up a counterclaim through oversight, inadvertence, or excusable neglect, or when justice requires he may by leave of court set up the counterclaim by amendment.

norms.heading: Cross-claims against coparty.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: A pleading may state as a cross-claim any claim by one party against a coparty arising out of the transaction or occurrence that is the subject matter either of the original action or of a counterclaim therein. Such cross-claim may include a claim that the party against whom it is asserted is or may be liable to the cross-claimant for all or part of a claim asserted in the action against the cross-claimant.

norms.heading: Additional parties made defendants when required for counterclaim or cross-claim.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: When the presence of parties other than those to the original action is required for the granting of complete relief in the determination of a counterclaim or cross-claim, the court shall order them to be brought in as defendants as provided in this code if jurisdiction of them can be obtained.

norms.heading: Reduction of assigned claims to the extent of all counterclaims.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: Except as otherwise provided by law as to negotiable instruments, every assigned claim shall be subject to be reduced to the extent of all counterclaims which the obligor had against the plaintiff's assignor at the time of notice of the assignment.

norms.heading: Amendment of pleadings.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: A party may amend his pleading as a matter of course at any time before a responsive pleading is filed and served, or, if the pleading is one to which no responsive pleading is required and the action has not been placed upon the trial calendar, he may so amend it at any time within thirty days after it is filed. Otherwise a party may amend his pleading only by leave of court or by written consent of the adverse party; and leave shall be freely given when justice so requires. A party shall plead in response to an amended pleading within the time remaining for response to the original pleading or within ten days after service of the amended pleading, whichever period may be the longer, unless the court otherwise orders.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article définit la demande additionnelle comme celle par laquelle une partie modifie ses prétentions antérieures. La Rule 55.33 et le RSMo 509.490 régissent la modification des actes de procédure, mais ajoutent des conditions de délai, de consentement ou d’autorisation judiciaire.
correspondences.note_en: The article defines an additional claim as one modifying a party’s prior claims. Rule 55.33 and RSMo 509.490 govern amendment of pleadings, but impose additional requirements concerning timing, consent, or leave of court.

norms.heading: Amendments to conform to evidence.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: When issues not raised by the pleadings are tried by express or implied consent of the parties, they shall be treated in all respects as if they had been raised in the pleadings. Such amendment of the pleadings as may be necessary to cause them to conform to the evidence and to raise these issues may be made upon motion of any party at any time, even after judgment; but failure so to amend does not affect the result of the trial of these issues. If evidence is objected to at the trial on the ground that it is not within the issues made by the pleadings, the court may allow the pleadings to be amended and shall do so freely when the presentation of the merits of the action will be subserved thereby and the objecting party fails to satisfy the court that the admission of such evidence would prejudice him in maintaining his action or defense upon the merits. The court may grant a continuance to enable the objecting party to meet such evidence.

norms.heading: Supplemental pleadings.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

norms.text: Upon motion of a party the court may, upon reasonable notice and upon such terms as are just, permit him to serve a supplemental pleading setting forth transactions or occurrences or events which have happened since the date of the pleading sought to be supplemented. If the court deems it advisable that the adverse party plead thereto, it shall so order, specifying the time therefor.

norms.heading: Court records, required redactions — confidential case file sheet, contents.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 509 Pleadings

revisor_notes: (2024) Subdivisions (4) and (5) of subsection 1 of section 509.520 requiring victim and witness names, addresses and contact information to be redacted in court filings are declared unconstitutional and thereby unenforceable as violating the First and Fourteenth Amendments of the United States Constitution and the Open Courts requirement of Article I, § 14 of the Missouri Constitution. Gross, et al. v. State of Missouri, Case No. 24AC-CC04658, December 20, 2024 (Circuit Court of Cole County)

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose en principe la chambre du conseil en matière familiale, avec publicité pour les décisions relatives au nom, au prénom et au divorce. Le Missouri permet d’exclure le public et de sceller certains dossiers de garde, et restreint l’accès à certains dossiers, sans règle générale identique.
correspondences.note_en: The article generally requires family matters to be heard in chambers, while decisions on names and divorce are public. Missouri permits exclusion of the public and sealing in custody proceedings and restricts access to certain records, but has no identical general rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose au greffier l’occultation de données identifiantes dans les décisions lorsque la sécurité ou la vie privée l’exige. Le § 509.520 vise notamment les jugements et ordonnances, le § 452.430 impose une occultation sur certaines copies de jugements, et le § 452.780 prévoit le scellement d’informations identifiantes en cas de risque, selon des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the clerk to redact identifying information in decisions when safety or privacy requires it. Section 509.520 covers judgments and orders, § 452.430 requires redaction on certain judgment copies, and § 452.780 provides for sealing identifying information where disclosure would create a risk, under different conditions.

norms.heading: Court may direct attorneys to appear before it for conference.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 8 permet au juge de demander aux parties les explications de fait nécessaires. Les dispositions Missouri prévoient des conférences dirigées par le tribunal pouvant notamment simplifier les questions et favoriser la clarification des faits et des documents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 8 permits the judge to request factual explanations needed to resolve the dispute. The Missouri provisions authorize court-directed conferences addressing simplification of issues and admissions concerning facts and documents, serving a comparable case-management function.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article autorise les avocats à conclure une convention d'instruction simplifiée. Le Missouri prévoit plutôt une conférence dirigée par le tribunal et une ordonnance reprenant les accords des parties, sans créer expressément une convention autonome entre avocats.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows the parties’ attorneys to enter an agreement for simplified case preparation. Missouri instead provides for a court-directed conference and an order reflecting the parties’ agreements, without expressly creating an autonomous attorney agreement.

correspondences.note_fr: Le président entend les avocats sur l'état de l'affaire et leur demande notamment s'ils envisagent une convention de mise en état. Les textes du Missouri prévoient une conférence de gestion examinant diverses questions procédurales, mais elle est facultative et ne vise pas spécifiquement cette convention.
correspondences.note_en: The president consults counsel about the procedural posture and specifically asks whether they contemplate a case-management agreement. The Missouri provisions allow a case-management conference addressing various procedural matters, but the conference is discretionary and does not specifically concern such an agreement.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 779 organise une ultime conférence d’orientation, les derniers échanges, la clôture de l’instruction ou le renvoi au juge de la mise en état, avec fixation d’audiences. Les Rules 62.01 et RSMo 510.010 prévoient des conférences de gestion et un ordre procédural, mais sans reprendre tout ce mécanisme; les autres dispositions concernent surtout les continuations et la fixation du procès.
correspondences.note_en: Article 779 governs a final case-orientation conference, last submissions, closing of the proceedings, or referral to the judge for case management, with hearings set as needed. Rules 62.01 and RSMo 510.010 provide comparable case-management conferences and controlling orders, but do not reproduce the full mechanism; the other provisions address continuances and trial settings.

norms.heading: Interrogatories to parties.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text:
1. Any party may serve upon any adverse party written interrogatories to be answered by the party served or, if the party served is a public or private corporation or a partnership or association, by any officer, director, partner or managing agent thereof competent to testify in its behalf.

2. The interrogatories shall be answered separately and fully in writing under oath. The answers shall be signed by the person making them; and the party upon whom the interrogatories have been served shall serve a copy of the answers on the party submitting the interrogatories within fifteen days after the delivery of the interrogatories, unless the court, on motion and notice and for good cause shown, enlarges or shortens the time.

3. Objections to any interrogatories may be presented to the court within ten days after service thereof, with notice as in case of a motion; and answers shall be deferred until the objections are determined, which shall be at as early a time as is practicable.

4. No party may, without leave of court, serve more than one set of interrogatories to be answered by the same party.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut entendre les mineurs, majeurs protégés, représentants de personnes morales et agents ou membres de celles-ci. La Rule 57.03(b)(4) prévoit la désignation de représentants d’une organisation pour une déposition, tandis que la Rule 52.02 et le RSMo 510.020 concernent respectivement la représentation des personnes vulnérables et l’interrogatoire des parties ou sociétés.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may examine minors, protected adults, representatives of legal entities, and their members or agents. Rule 57.03(b)(4) provides for organizational representatives to testify by deposition, while Rule 52.02 and RSMo 510.020 address representation of vulnerable persons and interrogatories to parties or entities.

norms.heading: Production of documents, papers, tangibles — statements previously made, definition, obtained, how.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text:
1. Upon motion of any party showing good cause therefor and upon notice to all other parties, the court in which an action is pending may:

(1) Order any party to produce and permit the inspection and copying or photographing, by or on behalf of the moving party, of* any designated documents, papers, books, accounts, letters, photographs, objects, or tangible things, not privileged, which constitute or contain evidence material to any matter involved in the action and which are in his possession, custody, or control; or

(2) Order any party to permit entry upon designated land or other property in his possession or control for the purpose of inspecting, measuring, surveying, sampling, or photographing the property or any designated relevant object or operation thereon. The order shall specify the time, place, and manner of making the inspection and taking the copies and photographs and may prescribe such terms and conditions as are just.

2. A party may obtain without the required showing a statement concerning the action or its subject matter previously made by that party. For purposes of this subsection, a statement previously made is a written statement signed or otherwise adopted or approved by the person making it, or a stenographic, mechanical, electrical, audio, video, motion picture or other recording, or a transcription thereof, of the party or of a statement made by the party and contemporaneously recorded.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article permet de demander au juge, sans forme, d'enjoindre la communication non effectuée. Le Missouri prévoit une demande de production et une motion visant à obtenir une ordonnance de contrainte, généralement avec des exigences procédurales et un préavis.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits an informal request for a judicial order compelling missing disclosure. Missouri provides document requests and motions to compel or enforce production, generally subject to specified procedural requirements and notice.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article permet au juge de fixer le délai et les modalités de communication, éventuellement sous astreinte. RSMo 510.030 prévoit que l'ordonnance précise le temps, le lieu et les modalités; les règles de discovery organisent les délais et sanctions, mais pas une astreinte équivalente.
correspondences.note_en: The article authorizes the judge to set the deadline and method of disclosure, potentially backed by a coercive penalty. RSMo 510.030 requires an order to specify time, place, and manner; discovery rules provide deadlines and sanctions but no equivalent astreinte.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 142 renvoie aux articles 138 et 139 pour les demandes et la production des éléments de preuve détenus par une partie. La Rule 58.01 prévoit directement les demandes de production entre parties, tandis que RSMo 510.030 organise une production ordonnée par le tribunal sur motion et pour bonne cause.
correspondences.note_en: Article 142 refers to Articles 138 and 139 for requests to produce evidence held by a party and for its production. Rule 58.01 directly governs party requests for production, while RSMo 510.030 provides for court-ordered production upon motion and a showing of good cause.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 275 impose la remise à l’expert des documents nécessaires et permet au juge d’en ordonner la production, avec des conséquences en cas de carence. Les Rules 58.01 et 61.01 prévoient respectivement la production et les sanctions en cas de non-respect. Le RSMo 510.030 prévoit la production sur ordonnance, sans sanction dans le texte fourni. Ces mécanismes ne sont pas spécifiques à l’expertise.
correspondences.note_en: Article 275 requires parties to provide necessary documents to the expert and permits an order compelling production, with consequences for noncompliance. Rules 58.01 and 61.01 address production and sanctions, respectively. RSMo 510.030 authorizes production by court order but states no sanction in the supplied text. None is expert-specific.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut ordonner la production de pièces de comparaison et faire composer des échantillons d’écriture. Rule 58.01 et RSMo 510.030 permettent d’ordonner la production et l’inspection de documents ou objets, mais ne réglementent pas spécifiquement les échantillons d’écriture ni la vérification graphologique.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may require comparison documents and dictated handwriting samples. Rule 58.01 and RSMo 510.030 authorize orders for production and inspection of documents or tangible things, but do not specifically regulate handwriting samples or judicial handwriting verification.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge conserve l’écrit contesté et les pièces de comparaison, ou en ordonne le dépôt au greffe. Les textes du Missouri permettent d’ordonner ou de demander la production et l’inspection de documents, mais ne prévoient pas ici leur dépôt au greffe pour vérification d’écriture.
correspondences.note_en: The judge retains the disputed writing and comparison materials or orders their filing with the clerk. Missouri provisions authorize court-ordered or requested production and inspection of documents, but do not provide for filing them with the clerk for handwriting verification.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut exiger la production de l’original papier lorsqu’un document a été établi sur papier. Le RSMo 510.030 permet d’ordonner à une partie de produire des documents, mais ne vise pas spécifiquement l’original papier. La Rule 81.21 concerne le dépôt de documents papier et non cette production.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may require production of the paper original when a document was created on paper. RSMo 510.030 permits an order requiring a party to produce documents, but does not specifically address paper originals. Rule 81.21 concerns filing paper documents, not compelled production.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge de la mise en état dispose de pouvoirs généraux pour communiquer, obtenir et faire produire les pièces. Les règles du Missouri organisent la discovery et la production par les parties ou par subpoena, avec des conditions et techniques différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The juge de la mise en état has broad powers to obtain and compel production of documents. Missouri Rules 56.01 and 58.02, together with RSMo 510.030, address discovery and document production through party requests, court orders, and subpoenas, but under materially different mechanisms and conditions.

norms.heading: Child victims of sexual offenses, video and aural recordings or photographs not subject to disclosure without court order — disclosure permitted, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

correspondences.note_fr: L’avocat peut obtenir copie du dossier, mais ne peut la communiquer au majeur, au mineur ou à un tiers. Le Missouri protège ou limite également l’accès et la reproduction de certains dossiers concernant les mineurs, mais dans des matières et selon des conditions plus étroites.
correspondences.note_en: Counsel may obtain copies of the case file but may not communicate them to the protected adult, minor, or a third party. Missouri likewise restricts access or reproduction of certain juvenile records, but only in narrower subject matters and under different conditions.

norms.heading: Court may order physical and mental examinations.
