path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: In an action in which the mental or physical condition of a party is in controversy, the court in which the action is pending may order him to submit to a physical or mental examination by a physician, chosen by the party requesting the examination. The order may be made only on motion for good cause shown and upon notice to the party to be examined and to all other parties not in default and shall specify the time, place, manner, conditions, and scope of the examination and the person or persons by whom it is to be made. Such physician shall be deemed the witness of the party procuring the examination unless called as a witness in court by the opposing party. Upon his request and without cost to himself the party examined shall be furnished by such order with a full written report of the examination.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut vérifier personnellement les faits litigieux, procéder à des constatations ou reconstitutions et se transporter sur les lieux. Les textes du Missouri permettent une expertise physique ou mentale ordonnée par le tribunal, mais non une vérification personnelle générale du juge.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may personally verify disputed facts, make observations or reconstructions, and visit the site. Missouri provisions authorize court-ordered physical or mental examinations, but not a general personal verification by the judge.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1212 permet au juge des tutelles et au procureur de faire examiner certains majeurs par un médecin. Les textes du Missouri permettent au tribunal d’ordonner un examen physique ou mental lorsque l’état de la personne est en cause, mais exigent une motion, un motif valable et un avis, sans conférer ce pouvoir au procureur.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1212 allows the tutorship judge and prosecutor to obtain a medical examination of certain adults. Missouri permits court-ordered physical or mental examinations when a person’s condition is in controversy, but requires a motion, good cause, and notice, and does not grant the stated authority to a prosecutor.

norms.heading: Request for admission of genuineness of relevant documents.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text:
1. At any time after the pleadings are closed, a party may serve upon any other party a written request for the admission by the latter of the genuineness of any relevant documents described in and exhibited with the request or of the truth of any relevant matters of fact pertaining to such documents set forth in the written request. Copies of the documents shall be delivered with the request unless copies have already been furnished. Each of the matters of which an admission is requested shall be deemed admitted unless, within a period designated in the request, not less than ten days after service thereof or within such further time as the court may allow on motion and notice, the party to whom the request is directed serves upon the party requesting the admission a sworn statement either denying specifically the matters of which an admission is requested or setting forth in detail the reasons why he cannot truthfully either admit or deny those matters.

2. Any admission made by a party pursuant to such request is for the purpose of the pending action only and neither constitutes an admission by him for any other purpose nor may it be used against him in any other proceeding.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 285 répartit la compétence pour la vérification incidente ou principale des écritures sous seing privé. Les règles 59.01 et 510.050 organisent les demandes d’admission de l’authenticité des documents, mais ne répartissent pas cette compétence entre juridictions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 285 allocates jurisdiction over incidental or principal verification of private writings. Rules 59.01 and 510.050 provide procedures for admitting the genuineness of documents, but do not allocate jurisdiction between courts.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge vérifie l’écriture ou la signature contestée, y compris électroniques, sauf inutilité. Les Rules 59.01 et RSMo 510.050 organisent surtout l’admission ou le refus de l’authenticité des documents, avec effet procédural, mais ne prévoient pas la vérification judiciaire de l’écriture elle-même.
correspondences.note_en: The court verifies disputed handwriting or signatures, including electronic ones, unless unnecessary. Rules 59.01 and RSMo 510.050 mainly provide for requests to admit or deny document genuineness and their procedural effects, but do not establish judicial handwriting verification itself.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 313 organise l’incident de faux soulevé devant une juridiction autre que le tribunal judiciaire ou la cour d’appel : sursis, exclusion éventuelle de la pièce et délai d’un mois pour saisir le tribunal judiciaire, à défaut de quoi la pièce est réputée reconnue. Les textes du Missouri prévoient seulement des mécanismes connexes d’admission ou de contestation de l’authenticité, sans cette procédure de faux ni ce sursis.
correspondences.note_en: Article 313 governs an incidental forgery challenge before a court other than the circuit court or court of appeal, including a stay, possible exclusion of the document, and a one-month deadline, failing which the document is deemed admitted. The Missouri provisions provide only related mechanisms for admitting or contesting genuineness, not this forgery procedure or stay.

norms.heading: Motion for order compelling answer to interrogatory.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text:
1. Upon the refusal of a party to answer any interrogatory submitted under section 510.020, the proponent of the question may move the court, on reasonable notice to all persons affected thereby, for an order compelling an answer. If the motion is granted and if the court finds that the refusal was without substantial justification the court shall require the refusing party to pay to the examining party the amount of the court costs incurred in obtaining the order. If the motion is denied and if the court finds that the motion was made without substantial justification, the court shall require the examining party to pay to the refusing party the amount of the court costs incurred in opposing the motion.

2. If any party or an officer, or general manager of a corporation refuses to obey an order made under subsection 1 requiring him to answer designated questions, or an order made under section 510.030 to produce any document or other thing for inspection, copying, or photographing, or to permit it to be done, or to permit entry upon land or other property, or an order made under section 510.040 requiring him to submit to a physical or mental examination, the court may make such orders in regard to the refusal as are just, and among others the following:

(1) An order that the matters regarding which the questions were asked or the character or description of the thing or land, or the contents of the paper, or the physical or mental condition of the party or any other designated facts shall be taken to be established for the purposes of the action in accordance with the claim of the party obtaining the order;

(2) An order refusing to allow the disobedient party to support or oppose designated claims or defenses, or prohibiting him from introducing in evidence designated documents or things or items of testimony, or from introducing evidence of physical or mental condition;

(3) An order striking out pleadings or parts thereof, or staying further proceedings until the order is obeyed, or dismissing the action or proceeding or any part thereof, or rendering a judgment by default against the disobedient party.

3. If a party, after being served with a request under section 510.050 to admit the genuineness of any documents or the truth of any relevant matters of fact pertaining to such documents, files and serves a written sworn denial thereof and if the party requesting the admissions thereafter proves the genuineness of any such document or the truth of any such matter of fact pertaining to such documents, he may apply to the court for an order requiring the other party to pay him the court costs incurred in making such proof. Unless the court finds that there were good reasons for the denial or that the admissions sought were of no substantial importance, the order shall be made.

4. If a party or an officer, or general manager of a corporation willfully fails to appear before the officer who is to take his deposition, after being served with a proper notice, or fails to return answers to interrogatories submitted under section 510.020, after proper service of such interrogatories, the court on motion and notice may strike out all or any part of any pleading of that party, or dismiss the action or proceeding or any part thereof, or enter a judgment by default against that party.
revisor_notes: (1977) Striking of pleadings and entry of default held proper where appellant twice refused to answer interrogatories. In re Marriage of Dickey (A.), 553 S.W.2d 518.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut tirer des conséquences juridiques des déclarations, de l’absence ou du refus de répondre, et assimiler ces éléments à un commencement de preuve par écrit. Les textes du Missouri autorisent surtout une inférence défavorable ou des sanctions procédurales, dans des procédures ou contextes plus limités.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may draw legal consequences from statements, absence, or refusal to answer, and treat them as equivalent to a beginning of written proof. Missouri provisions mainly authorize adverse inferences or procedural sanctions, in more limited proceedings or contexts.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 295 sanctionne le déni injustifié d’une écriture ou signature par une amende civile pouvant atteindre 10 000 euros, sans préjudice de dommages-intérêts. RSMo 510.060 prévoit, en cas de preuve de l’authenticité malgré un déni sous serment, le remboursement des frais, tandis que Rule 55.03 permet des sanctions générales pour des assertions ou dénégations injustifiées.
correspondences.note_en: Article 295 sanctions an unjustified denial of authorship or signature with a civil fine of up to €10,000, without prejudice to damages. RSMo 510.060 provides costs when authenticity is proved despite a sworn denial, while Rule 55.03 allows general sanctions for unjustified factual assertions or denials.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 299 organise l’examen judiciaire d’un écrit sous seing privé argué de faux en renvoyant aux articles 287 à 295. Le RSMo 510.060(3) prévoit la contestation et la preuve de l’authenticité d’un document, avec une éventuelle imputation des frais; la Rule 59.01 encadre les admissions relatives à l’authenticité, sans organiser l’incident de faux lui-même.
correspondences.note_en: Article 299 directs the court to examine a private writing alleged to be forged under Articles 287–295. RSMo 510.060(3) addresses denial and proof of a document’s genuineness, with possible costs, while Rule 59.01 governs admissions concerning genuineness but does not establish a forgery incident procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 313 organise l’incident de faux soulevé devant une juridiction autre que le tribunal judiciaire ou la cour d’appel : sursis, exclusion éventuelle de la pièce et délai d’un mois pour saisir le tribunal judiciaire, à défaut de quoi la pièce est réputée reconnue. Les textes du Missouri prévoient seulement des mécanismes connexes d’admission ou de contestation de l’authenticité, sans cette procédure de faux ni ce sursis.
correspondences.note_en: Article 313 governs an incidental forgery challenge before a court other than the circuit court or court of appeal, including a stay, possible exclusion of the document, and a one-month deadline, failing which the document is deemed admitted. The Missouri provisions provide only related mechanisms for admitting or contesting genuineness, not this forgery procedure or stay.

norms.heading: Cases shall be placed on docket, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: As soon as possible after issue is joined in a case pending in circuit court or after ten days from the date a case reaches the trial court upon appeal, by change of venue or otherwise upon issue already joined, the clerk shall place the same upon the trial docket. Cases shall be set for trial in accordance with the rules and practice of the trial court except as such appeals may be otherwise especially provided for by law.

correspondences.note_fr: Le président renvoie les affaires en état à l'audience, clôt l'instruction et fixe la date de plaidoirie, avec une procédure particulière en cas de jugement sans audience. Les textes du Missouri régissent la mise au rôle et la fixation du procès, mais ne prévoient pas l'ensemble de ces mécanismes ni la clôture française de l'instruction.
correspondences.note_en: The president sends trial-ready cases to the hearing, closes the preparatory phase, and sets the trial date, with a special procedure for determination without a hearing. The Missouri provisions govern docketing and trial settings, but do not provide all of these mechanisms or the French form of closing the proceedings.

norms.heading: Court may continue an action to a fixed day.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: For good cause shown, the court may continue an action to a fixed day, or to a date for trial to be set thereafter. Every continuance granted on the application of a party may be at the cost of such party, if so ordered by the court.

correspondences.note_fr: La conclusion de la convention interrompt, sous condition, le délai de péremption de l'instance, sans dessaisir le juge, qui conserve compétence pour les incidents, exceptions, fins de non-recevoir et mesures provisoires. Les textes du Missouri couvrent certaines défenses et objections procédurales, leur présentation et la continuation de l'instance, mais non l'interruption conventionnelle de la péremption ni l'ensemble de ces effets.
correspondences.note_en: The agreement conditionally interrupts the procedural expiration period while preserving the judge’s authority over procedural incidents, objections, defenses, and provisional measures. Missouri addresses some procedural defenses and objections, their presentation, and continuances, but not convention-based interruption of the expiration period or all of these effects.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit le renvoi de l’affaire à une audience ultérieure et l’information des parties sur les audiences suivantes. Les Rules 65.01 et 55.30 ainsi que le RSMo 510.080 concernent les continuances et l’organisation des audiences, mais sans reprendre l’ensemble du mécanisme français.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides for continuation to a later hearing and notice of subsequent hearings. Rules 65.01 and 55.30 and RSMo 510.080 address continuances and hearing arrangements, but do not reproduce the full French mechanism.

norms.heading: Application for continuance, how made.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: Every application for a continuance shall, unless the adverse party consent that it be made orally in open court, be made by motion in writing, accompanied by the affidavit of the applicant, or of some other credible person, setting forth the facts on which the application is founded.

norms.heading: Applications for a continuance on account of absence of witnesses shall show what.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.heading: Amendment of affidavit — overruled, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: If the court shall be of the opinion that the affidavit is insufficient, it shall permit the same to be amended; and if after such amendment the affidavit does not contain a sufficient statement of facts as herein required, the court shall overrule the same; but if, upon the contrary, the court shall find the affidavit sufficient, the cause shall be continued, unless the opposite party will admit that the witness, if present, would swear to the facts set out in said affidavit, in which event the cause shall not be continued, but the party moving therefor shall read as the evidence of such witness the facts so stated in such affidavit and the opposing party may disprove the facts disclosed, or prove any contradictory statements made by such absent witness in relation to the matter in issue and on trial.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise la preuve contraire sans nouvelle décision après l’ordonnance d’enquête. RSMo 510.110 permet, dans le contexte particulier d’un affidavit d’un témoin absent, de contester les faits exposés ou d’en prouver les déclarations contradictoires sans continuation de l’instance.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits contrary proof without a new decision after an inquiry is ordered. RSMo 510.110, in the specific context of an absent witness’s affidavit, permits the opposing party to disprove the disclosed facts or prove contradictory statements without a continuance.

norms.heading: Automatic stay of all administrative and court procedures for members of the general assembly, when — continuance when counsel or party is a member of general assembly.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text:
1. During the period beginning January first and ending June first of each year, or whenever the general assembly is in session, there shall be an automatic stay of all administrative and court proceedings in which any member of the general assembly has filed a written notice with the court or administrative hearing officer and with all parties to the proceeding that the member is:

(1) A necessary witness;

(2) A party to the action; or

(3) The initial attorney for any party or has filed an entry of appearance as an attorney for any party more than forty-five days prior to the filing of the written notice under this subsection.

2. The stay created by this section shall apply to all trials, motions, hearings, discovery responses, depositions, responses to motions, docket calls, and any other proceedings before any trial court or administrative tribunal, including municipal courts. The stay shall also apply to any order requiring the member to serve as a juror whenever the general assembly is in session.

3. The stay created by this section shall not apply:

(1) If the member waives the protections of this stay in the form of a written memorandum filed with the trial court or administrative tribunal;

(2) To any proceedings under chapter 288;

(3) To any proceedings involving a request for injunctive relief; or

(4) To any proceeding in which the member is charged with a felony or a class A misdemeanor.

4. The court of appeals shall have original jurisdiction over any application for termination or modification of the stay.

5. In all civil cases or administrative proceedings or in criminal cases pending in this state at any time when the general assembly is in veto session, special session, or holding out-of-session committee hearings, it shall be a sufficient cause for such continuance if it shall appear to the court, by written notice, that any party applying for such continuance, or any attorney, solicitor or counsel of such party is a member of either house of the general assembly, and in actual attendance on the out-of-session committee hearings, special session, or veto session of the same, and that the attendance of such party, attorney, solicitor or counsel is necessary to a fair and proper trial or other proceeding in such suit; and on the filing of such notice the court shall continue such suit and any and all motions or other proceedings therein, of every kind and nature, including the taking of depositions and discovery responses, and thereupon no trial or other proceedings of any kind or nature shall be had therein until the adjournment or recess for three days or more of the special session or veto session of the general assembly, nor for one day before or after or the day of any out-of-session committee hearings. Such notice shall be sufficient, if made within two days of the out-of-session committee hearings, special session, or veto session of the general assembly, showing that at the time of making the same such party, attorney, solicitor or counsel is scheduled to be in actual attendance upon such out-of-session committee hearings, special session, or veto session of the general assembly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 377 prévoit que l’instance est suspendue par une décision de sursis, de radiation ou de retrait du rôle, sauf disposition légale contraire. Le Missouri connaît des suspensions ou continuations de l’instance, mais dans des contextes et selon des conditions spécifiques, sans reprendre ces trois mécanismes de manière générale.
correspondences.note_en: Article 377 provides that proceedings are suspended by an order staying, striking, or removing the case from the docket, unless otherwise provided by law. Missouri provides stays or continuances in specific contexts and subject to particular conditions, but does not generally reproduce all three mechanisms.

correspondences.note_fr: Le tribunal arbitral peut suspendre l’instance pour une durée ou jusqu’à un événement, puis révoquer ou abréger le sursis. Les textes du Missouri prévoient des suspensions ou continuations judiciaires comparables, mais dans des contextes déterminés et sans le même pouvoir général du tribunal arbitral.
correspondences.note_en: An arbitral tribunal may stay proceedings for a specified period or until an event, and may revoke or shorten the stay. The Missouri provisions provide comparable stays or continuances, but only in specified judicial contexts and without the same general arbitral power.

norms.heading: Grievance resolution system for offenders, civil actions stayed, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text:
1. In any civil action brought in a court of this state by an offender convicted of a crime who is confined in any state prison or correctional facility, the court shall stay such case until the offender has exhausted such administrative remedies as are described in this section and are available to the offender.

2. The department of corrections shall maintain a system or systems for the resolution of grievances of offenders confined in each state prison or correctional facility. The systems may provide for:

(1) Time limits for replies to grievances at each decision level within the system;

(2) Priority processing of grievances which are of an emergency nature, including matters in which delay would subject the grievant to substantial risk of personal injury;

(3) Safeguards to avoid reprisals against any grievant or participant in the resolution of a grievance; and

(4) Review of the disposition of grievances by a person or other entity who did not render the original decision of the grievance.

3. Notwithstanding the provisions of subsections 1 and 2 of this section, the provisions of any federal statute governing a cause of action created by federal law shall control and take precedence in actions brought pursuant to such federal law.

norms.heading: Voluntary dismissal — new trial.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text:
1. A plaintiff shall be allowed to dismiss his action without prejudice at any time before the same is finally submitted to the jury, or to the court sitting as a jury, or to the court, and not afterward. A plaintiff who has once so dismissed his action and thereafter files another action upon the same claim shall not be allowed to dismiss the same without prejudice after the jury has been impaneled, or after evidence has been introduced in a nonjury case, except

(1) Upon filing a stipulation to that effect signed by the opposite party; or

(2) On order of the court made on special motion in which the ground for said dismissal shall be set forth and which shall be supported by affidavit.

2. No party, who has been granted a dismissal at his request after an adverse ruling of the trial court preventing a recovery on his part, shall as a matter of right be granted more than one new trial or more than one appeal on the ground that the adverse ruling of the trial court preventing a recovery on his part was erroneous.
revisor_notes: (1972) Plaintiff does not have an absolute right to take a voluntary dismissal but to deny such dismissal, defendant must show some injury to himself more than the mere fact that plaintiff could bring another action. Stubblefield v. Seals (Mo.), 485 S.W.2d 126.

correspondences.note_fr: Le demandeur peut se désister de sa demande, en toute matière, afin de mettre fin à l’instance. Le Missouri autorise également le désistement volontaire, mais le droit de le faire sans ordonnance judiciaire est limité à certains stades de la procédure.
correspondences.note_en: The plaintiff may withdraw the claim in any matter to terminate the action. Missouri likewise permits voluntary dismissal, but the right to dismiss without a court order is limited to specified procedural stages.

correspondences.note_fr: Le désistement est en principe subordonné à l’acceptation du défendeur, sauf absence de défense au fond ou de fin de non-recevoir. Les dispositions du Missouri régissent le désistement volontaire et prévoient notamment une stipulation de la partie adverse dans certains cas, sans reprendre cette règle générale d’acceptation.
correspondences.note_en: Withdrawal generally requires the defendant’s acceptance, unless the defendant has asserted no defense on the merits or objection to admissibility. Missouri regulates voluntary dismissal and requires an opposing-party stipulation in limited circumstances, but has no equivalent general acceptance requirement.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge doit déclarer le désistement parfait lorsque le refus du défendeur n’est pas fondé sur un motif légitime. Au Missouri, lorsque le désistement n’est pas un droit unilatéral, il nécessite une ordonnance judiciaire, mais le texte ne prévoit pas le critère du motif légitime du refus.
correspondences.note_en: The judge must declare the withdrawal effective when the defendant’s refusal lacks a legitimate reason. In Missouri, a voluntary dismissal outside the unilateral-dismissal period requires a court order, but the supplied texts do not adopt the French standard concerning the legitimacy of the refusal.

norms.heading: Defendant may move for dismissal of an action — effect of motion.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: For failure of the plaintiff to prosecute or to comply with this code or any order of court, a defendant may move for dismissal of an action or of any claim against him. After the plaintiff has completed the presentation of his evidence, the defendant, without waiving his right to offer evidence in the event the motion is not granted, or in the event that the motion is granted and the resulting judgment is later held erroneous, may move for a dismissal on the ground that upon the facts and the law the plaintiff has shown no right to relief.

norms.heading: Effect of dismissals, with and without prejudice.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: A dismissal without prejudice permits the party to bring another action for the same cause, unless the action is otherwise barred. A dismissal with prejudice operates as an adjudication upon the merits. Any voluntary dismissal other than one which the party is entitled to take without prejudice, and any involuntary dismissal other than one for lack of jurisdiction or for improper venue shall be with prejudice unless the court in its order for dismissal shall otherwise specify.

correspondences.note_fr: Le désistement éteint l’instance sans renoncer à l’action. Les dismissals without prejudice du Missouri permettent d’engager une nouvelle action pour la même cause, sous réserve des règles applicables et de certaines limites procédurales.
correspondences.note_en: Withdrawal ends the proceeding without waiving the underlying action. Missouri dismissals without prejudice permit another action for the same cause, subject to applicable bars and procedural limitations.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit l’extinction de l’instance en cas de non-comparution ou de défaut de constitution d’avocat et rend non avenue l’ordonnance. Les textes du Missouri permettent le rejet et en précisent les effets, mais ne prévoient pas cette extinction ni l’anéantissement de l’ordonnance.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides for termination when the parties fail to appear or the creditor fails to obtain counsel, and renders the payment order ineffective. Missouri provisions allow dismissal and specify its effects, but do not provide for this specific termination or nullification of the order.

norms.heading: Provisions applying to dismissal of counterclaim, cross-claim or third-party claim.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: The provisions of sections 510.130 to 510.150 and 514.180, apply to the dismissal of any counterclaim, cross-claim, or third-party claim.

norms.heading: Dismissal of plaintiff's action not to affect counterclaim or cross-claim.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: No dismissal, voluntary or involuntary, of a plaintiff's action in which a counterclaim or cross-claim has been filed shall operate to dismiss or discontinue such counterclaim or cross-claim.

norms.heading: Consolidation of actions — separate trials of issues.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text:
1. Whenever several suits founded alone upon liquidated demands shall be pending in the same court by the same plaintiff, against the same defendant, or whenever several such suits are pending in the same court, by the same plaintiff, against several defendants, the court in which the same shall be prosecuted may, in its discretion, if it appear expedient, order such suits to be consolidated into one action.

2. The court in furtherance of convenience or to avoid prejudice may order a separate trial of any claim, cross-claim, counterclaim, or third-party claim, or of any separate issue or of any number of claims, cross-claims, counterclaims, third-party claims, or issues.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut joindre plusieurs instances liées. La Rule 66.01 et le RSMo 510.180 prévoient la consolidation ; la Rule 52.06 permet de séparer une demande contre une partie. Ces textes ne reproduisent pas exactement la disjonction générale d’une instance en plusieurs.
correspondences.note_en: The court may consolidate related actions. Rule 66.01 and RSMo 510.180 provide for consolidation; Rule 52.06 allows a claim against a party to be severed. These provisions do not exactly reproduce the general severance of one action into several.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge de la mise en état ordonne les jonctions et disjonctions d'instance. Les Rules 66.01 et 66.02, ainsi que le RSMo 510.180, prévoient respectivement la consolidation d'actions et la tenue de procès séparés, mais avec des conditions et effets plus détaillés.
correspondences.note_en: The juge de la mise en état orders the consolidation or severance of proceedings. Rules 66.01 and 66.02, and RSMo 510.180, respectively provide for consolidation and separate trials, but with more detailed conditions and effects.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge chargé d'instruire l'affaire procède aux jonctions et disjonctions d'instance. Les dispositions du Missouri permettent au tribunal de consolider des actions et d'ordonner des procès séparés, mais n'établissent pas un juge de l'instruction de type français ni un mécanisme identique de disjonction.
correspondences.note_en: The assigned judge conducts consolidation and severance of proceedings. Missouri provisions allow the court to consolidate actions and order separate trials, but do not establish a French-style pretrial judge or an identical severance mechanism.

norms.heading: Right of trial by jury — waiver.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

revisor_notes: (1973) Held that trial by jury cannot be waived by informal statement by counsel that jury would not be required. Randolph v. Simpson (A.), 500 S.W.2d 289.
(1974) Held wife's counterclaim for necessaries was a claim at law and jury trial must be granted. Attebery v. Attebery (A.), 507 S.W.2d 87.

norms.heading: All trials upon the merits shall be conducted in open court.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: All trials upon the merits shall be conducted in open court and so far as convenient in the regular courtroom. Trials may be conducted or motions heard outside the county where pending with the consent of all parties affected thereby.

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC pose la publicité des débats comme principe, avec des exceptions légales de huis clos ou de chambre du conseil. Les règles du Missouri exigent surtout que les procès au fond se tiennent en audience publique, tandis que certaines procédures, notamment celles visées par le RSMo 210.846, se tiennent à huis clos.
correspondences.note_en: The CPC makes public hearings the general rule, subject to statutory exceptions for closed hearings. Missouri requires trials on the merits to be held in open court, while allowing other proceedings in chambers and requiring closed hearings in the proceedings covered by RSMo 210.846.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article pose la publicité des débats, sous réserve des exceptions légales, et impose en appel la règle applicable en première instance. Le Missouri prévoit l’ouverture des procès au fond, avec des exceptions particulières, notamment en matière de garde d’enfants et de protection de l’enfance, sans reprendre la règle générale de l’appel.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes public hearings subject to statutory exceptions and carries the first-instance rule into appeals. Missouri requires trials on the merits to be open, with specific exceptions for custody and child-protection matters, but does not reproduce the general appellate carryover rule.

norms.heading: Formal exceptions unnecessary — objections.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: Formal exceptions to rulings or orders of the court are unnecessary; but for all purposes for which an exception has heretofore been necessary it is sufficient that a party, at the time the ruling or order of the court is made or sought, makes known to the court the action which he desires the court to take or his objection to the action of the court and his grounds therefor except it shall not be necessary to state grounds for objections for instructions; and, if a party has no opportunity to object to a ruling or order at the time it is made, the absence of an objection does not thereafter prejudice him.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 446 prévoit la nullité de certaines irrégularités, leur invocation avant la clôture et l’absence de relevé d’office. Les textes du Missouri cités concernent plutôt la formulation et la préservation des objections ou erreurs pour l’appel, sans prévoir ces mêmes effets de nullité.
correspondences.note_en: Article 446 makes specified irregularities subject to nullity, requires invocation before closing, and bars the court from raising nullity sua sponte. The cited Missouri provisions instead address stating and preserving objections or errors for appellate review, without providing the same nullity effects.

norms.heading: Verdict, general or special.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: The verdict of a jury is either general or special. A general verdict is one by which the jury pronounces generally upon all or any of the issues, either in favor of the plaintiff or defendant. A special verdict is one by which the jury finds the facts only, leaving the judgment to the court.

norms.heading: General verdict, when rendered.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: In every issue for the recovery of money only, or specific real or personal property, the jury shall render a general verdict.

norms.heading: Court may direct issues to be made, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: In all other cases, if at any time during the progress of any cause, it shall, in the opinion of the court, become necessary to determine any fact in controversy by the verdict of a jury, the court may direct an issue or issues to be made.

norms.heading: Issues to be made only as directed by court.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: No issue shall be made, except such as shall be directed by the court.

norms.heading: Issues, how tried and disposed of.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: The trial of such issues shall be by jury, and the issues shall be disposed of by a general or special verdict before a final judgment shall be made therein.

norms.heading: Punitive damages, restrictions on award of — proper award, when — civil actions, initial pleading not to contain claim for punitive damage award.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text:
1. Except as otherwise provided by statute, punitive damages shall not be awarded unless the claimant proves by clear and convincing evidence that the defendant intentionally harmed the plaintiff without just cause or acted with a deliberate and flagrant disregard for the safety of others.

2. Punitive damages may only be recovered if the trier of fact awards more than nominal damages or if the claim or claims for which nominal damages are solely awarded invoke privacy rights, property rights, or rights protected by the Constitution of the United States or the Constitution of the state of Missouri.

3. Punitive damages can properly be awarded against an employer or other principal because of an act by an agent if, but only if:

(1) The principal or a managerial agent of the principal authorized the doing and the manner of the act;

(2) The agent was unfit and the principal or a managerial agent of the principal was reckless in employing or retaining him or her;

(3) The agent was employed in a managerial capacity and was acting in the scope of employment; or

(4) The principal or a managerial agent of the principal ratified or approved the act.

4. When an employer admits liability for the actions of an agent in a claim for compensatory damages, the court shall grant limited discovery consisting only of employment records and documents or information related to the agent's qualifications.

5. No initial pleading in a civil action shall contain a claim for a punitive damage award. Any later pleading containing a claim for a punitive damage award may be filed only with leave of the court. A trial court may grant leave to file such a pleading only on written motion by the claimant, filed no later than one hundred twenty days prior to the final pretrial conference in the case or, if there is no scheduled pretrial conference, one hundred twenty days prior to the date set for trial, that is supported by affidavits, exhibits, or discovery materials establishing a reasonable basis for recovery of punitive damages. Any party opposing leave may file affidavits, exhibits, or discovery materials demonstrating that the standards for a punitive damage award pursuant to this section have not been established. If the trial court concludes, following its review of all materials submitted in connection with the motion, that based on the evidence to be admitted at trial a trier of fact could reasonably conclude, based on clear and convincing evidence, that the standards for a punitive damage award contained in this section have been met, the court shall grant leave to file the pleading seeking a punitive damage award. The court shall rule on a motion for leave to file a pleading seeking punitive damages no later than forty-five days after a hearing on the motion or, if no hearing is held on the motion, after the party opposing the motion has filed its response to the motion. The responsive pleading shall be limited to responding to the newly amended punitive damages claim.

6. The amount of punitive damages shall not be based, in whole or in part, on harm to nonparties.

7. No judgment that includes a punitive damage award shall be entered in any civil action in any court of this state, or in any court in which claims are asserted based on the constitution, statutes, or common law of this state, unless the requirements and procedures for a punitive damage award contained in this section and sections 510.263 and 537.675 are met.

8. Except to the extent that they are expressly inconsistent with this section, all common law limitations on punitive damages and all limitations on the recovery of punitive damages contained in other sections of the laws of this state remain in full force and effect.

9. As used in this section, the term "punitive damage award" means an award for punitive or exemplary damages or an award for aggravating circumstances.
revisor_notes: Applicability of statute changes for cases filed after August 28, 2020, 510.262

norms.heading: Applicability of certain statute changes for cases filed after August 28, 2020.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: The provisions of this act* shall apply to causes of action filed on or after August 28, 2020.
revisor_notes: * "This act" contained numerous sections. Consult Disposition of Sections table for a definitive listing.

norms.heading: Bifurcated trial, when, procedure — post-trial motion for credit on punitive damages, procedure — credit not allowed, when — doctrine of remittitur and additur applied to awards — discovery.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text:
1. All actions tried before a jury involving punitive damages, including tort actions based upon improper health care, shall be conducted in a bifurcated trial before the same jury if requested by any party.

2. In the first stage of a bifurcated trial, in which the issue of punitive damages is submissible, the jury shall determine liability for compensatory damages, the amount of compensatory damages, including nominal damages, and the liability of a defendant for punitive damages. Evidence of defendant's financial condition shall not be admissible in the first stage of such trial unless admissible for a proper purpose other than the amount of punitive damages.

3. If during the first stage of a bifurcated trial the jury determines that a defendant is liable for punitive damages, that jury shall determine, in a second stage of trial, the amount of punitive damages to be awarded against such defendant. Evidence of such defendant's net worth shall be admissible during the second stage of such trial.

4. Within the time for filing a motion for new trial, a defendant may file a post-trial motion requesting the amount awarded by the jury as punitive damages be credited by the court with amounts previously paid in any state or federal court by the defendant for punitive damages arising out of the same conduct on which the imposition of punitive damages is based. At any hearing, the burden on all issues relating to such a credit shall be on the defendant and either party may introduce relevant evidence on such motion. Such a motion shall be determined by the trial court within the time and according to procedures applicable to motions for new trial. If the trial court sustains such a motion the trial court shall credit the jury award of punitive damages by the amount found by the trial court to have been previously paid by the defendant arising out of the same conduct and enter judgment accordingly. If the defendant fails to establish entitlement to a credit under the provisions of this section, or the trial court finds from the evidence that the defendant's conduct out of which the prior punitive damage award arose was not the same conduct on which the imposition of punitive damages is based in the pending action, or the trial court finds the defendant unreasonably continued the conduct after acquiring actual knowledge of the dangerous nature of such conduct, the trial court shall disallow such credit, or, if the trial court finds that the laws regarding punitive damages in the state or federal court in which the prior award of punitive damages was entered substantially and materially deviate from the law of the state of Missouri, except with respect to section 537.675, and that the nature of such deviation provides good cause for disallowance of the credit based on the public policy of Missouri, then the trial court may disallow all or any part of the credit provided by this section.

5. The credit allowable under this section shall not apply to causes of action for libel, slander, assault, battery, false imprisonment, criminal conversation, malicious prosecution or fraud.

6. The doctrines of remittitur and additur, based on the trial judge's assessment of the totality of the surrounding circumstances, shall apply to punitive damage awards.

7. As used in this section, "punitive damage award" means an award for punitive or exemplary damages or an award for aggravating circumstances.

8. Discovery as to a defendant's assets shall be allowed only after a trial court has granted leave to file a pleading seeking punitive damages in accordance with subsection 5 of section 510.261.
revisor_notes: Applicability of statute changes for cases filed after August 28, 2005, 538.305; for cases filed after August 28, 2020, 510.262

norms.heading: Limitations on punitive damages in certain cases.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text:
1. No award of punitive damages against any defendant shall exceed the greater of:

(1) Five hundred thousand dollars; or

(2) Five times the net amount of the judgment awarded to the plaintiff against the defendant.

Such limitations shall not apply if the state of Missouri is the plaintiff requesting the award of punitive damages, or the defendant pleads guilty to or is convicted of a felony arising out of the acts or omissions pled by the plaintiff.

2. The provisions of this section and sections 510.261 and 510.263 shall not apply to civil actions brought under section 213.111 that allege a violation of section 213.040, 213.045, 213.050, or 213.070, to the extent that the alleged violation of section 213.070 relates to or involves a violation of section 213.040, 213.045, or 213.050, or subdivision (3) of subsection 1 of section 213.070 as it relates to housing.
revisor_notes: Applicability of statute changes for cases filed after August 28, 2005, 538.305; for cases filed after August 28, 2020, 510.262

(2014) Section's cap on punitive damage awards is unconstitutional under Article I, Section 22 (a) of Missouri Constitution; right to a jury trial in 1820 included right to have a jury determine amount of punitive damages in an action for fraud. Lewellen v. Franklin, 441 S.W.3d 136 (Mo.banc).

norms.heading: Jury shall assess amount of money of recovery, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: When a verdict shall be found for the plaintiff in an action for the recovery of money only, the jury shall also assess the amount of the recovery; so, also, if they find for the defendant in case of offsets or other demand for money. When exemplary or punitive damages are allowed by the jury, the amount thereof shall be separately stated in the verdict.

norms.heading: Motion for directed verdict.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: The demurrer to the evidence and the request for peremptory instructions are abolished and in lieu thereof a party may make a motion for a directed verdict. A party who moves for a directed verdict at the close of the evidence offered by an opponent may offer evidence in the event that the motion is not granted, without having reserved the right so to do and to the same extent as if the motion had not been made. A motion for a directed verdict which is not granted is not a waiver of trial by jury even though all parties to the action have moved for directed verdicts. Upon motion for directed verdict by a party opposing a claim the court, whether so requested or not, may dismiss the claim without prejudice if justice so requires.

norms.heading: Denial of motion for directed verdict — motion to set aside verdict, judgment — motion for new trial.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: Whenever a motion for a directed verdict made at the close of all the evidence is denied or for any reason is not granted the court is deemed to have submitted the action to the jury subject to a later determination of the legal questions raised by the motion. Within ten days after the reception of a verdict, a party who has moved for a directed verdict may move to have the verdict and any judgment entered thereon set aside and to have judgment entered in accordance with his motion for a directed verdict; or if a verdict was not returned, such party, within ten days after the jury has been discharged, may move for judgment in accordance with his motion for a directed verdict. A motion for a new trial may be joined with this motion, or a new trial may be prayed for in the alternative. If a verdict was returned the court may allow the judgment to stand or may reopen the judgment and either order a new trial or direct the entry of judgment as if the requested verdict had been directed. If no verdict was returned the court may direct the entry of judgment as if the requested verdict had been directed or may order a new trial.

norms.heading: Instructions.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text:
1. At the close of all the evidence, or at such earlier time during the trial as the court may reasonably direct, any party may request that the court instruct the jury in writing on the law applicable to the issues in evidence in the case. Such instructions so requested to be submitted in writing by the party requesting the same, and may be given or refused by the court according to the law and the evidence in the case. The court may also instruct the jury in writing of its own motion. The court shall afford ample opportunity for counsel to examine the instructions before the same are given and to make objections out of the hearing of the jury.

2. Instructions which are refused shall be so marked by the court and filed with the clerk. All instructions given shall be carried by the jury to their room and returned and filed at the conclusion of their deliberations. All instructions refused and all instructions given shall be kept as part of the record of the cause.

norms.heading: Procedure in cases tried upon facts without a jury.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text:
1. In cases tried upon the facts without a jury, the court shall rule upon all objections to evidence as in jury cases. Where the court is of the opinion that the evidence is not admissible, it shall not receive the evidence, but where the evidence is brief and is not privileged, the court shall permit the same and any cross-examination relating thereto or evidence in rebuttal thereof to be taken down by the court reporter or otherwise preserved, apart from the evidence received.

2. At or after the trial, the court shall render such judgment as it thinks right upon the law and the evidence. If any party shall so request before final submission of the case, the court shall dictate to the court reporter, or prepare and file a brief opinion containing a statement of the grounds for its decision and the method of determining any damages awarded; and may, or if specifically requested by counsel, shall, include its findings on any of the principal controverted fact issues. All fact issues upon which no specific findings are made shall be deemed found in accordance with the result reached.

3. Upon motion of a party made not later than ten days after entry of judgment the court may amend the judgment and opinion. The motion may be made with a motion for a new trial.

4. No findings of fact, except such as shall have been specifically requested, and no conclusions of law or objections to the judgment or to the opinion of the court are necessary for purposes of review. The question of the sufficiency of the evidence to support the judgment may be raised whether or not the question was raised in the trial court. The appellate court shall review the case upon both the law and the evidence as in suits of an equitable nature. The judgment shall not be set aside unless clearly erroneous, and due regard shall be given to the opportunity of the trial court to judge of the credibility of the witnesses. The appellate court shall consider any evidence which was rejected by the trial court and duly preserved for the appeal when the appellate court believes such evidence to be admissible. The appellate court may also order any rejected evidence to be taken by deposition or under a reference and returned to said court.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 26 autorise le juge statuant gracieusement à fonder sa décision sur tous les faits pertinents, même non allégués. RSMo 510.310 permet de statuer selon le droit et les preuves, tandis que les dispositions relatives à l’adoption imposent la prise en compte d’informations pertinentes, sans reprendre expressément la règle des faits non allégués.
correspondences.note_en: Article 26 permits the judge in a non-contentious matter to rely on all relevant facts, including facts not alleged. RSMo 510.310 permits judgment on the law and evidence, and the adoption provisions require consideration of pertinent information, but none expressly authorizes reliance on unalleged facts.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 182 impose un procès-verbal des constatations, évaluations, appréciations, reconstitutions ou déclarations du juge, sauf mention au jugement dans un cas limité. Le RSMo 510.310 prévoit la consignation d’une opinion et, sur demande, de constatations de fait dans les affaires jugées sans jury, mais ne règle pas spécifiquement le procès-verbal des vérifications personnelles.
correspondences.note_en: Article 182 requires a record of the judge’s observations, evaluations, reconstructions, or statements, subject to a limited judgment-entry exception. RSMo 510.310 provides for written opinions and, on request, findings of fact in bench-tried cases, but does not specifically govern a record of the judge’s personal verifications.

correspondences.note_fr: Les parties peuvent invoquer des moyens nouveaux et produire de nouvelles pièces ou preuves pour soutenir en appel leurs prétentions initiales. Les textes du Missouri permettent surtout l'examen de preuves rejetées mais conservées, notamment dans les procès sans jury; ils ne consacrent pas une faculté générale de présenter des moyens, pièces ou preuves nouveaux.
correspondences.note_en: Parties may raise new arguments and submit new documents or evidence to support claims made below. Missouri primarily permits review of rejected but preserved evidence, especially in bench trials; the supplied texts do not establish a general right to introduce new arguments, documents, or evidence on appeal.

norms.heading: Trial or proceeding shall not be terminated by expiration of term.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: No trial or proceeding in any civil or criminal case shall be terminated by the expiration of the term at which it was commenced, but such trial or proceeding may proceed until it is concluded in all respects as if the term had not expired, or same may be continued to an adjourned or special term, or to the next regular term, as the court may direct.

norms.heading: Granting of new trial.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: A new trial may be granted for any of the reasons for which new trials have heretofore been granted. A new trial may be granted to all or any of the parties and on all or part of the issues after trial by jury, court or referee. On a motion for a new trial in an action tried without a jury, the court may open the judgment if one has been entered, take additional testimony, amend findings of fact or make new findings, and direct the entry of a new judgment. Only one new trial shall be allowed on the ground that the verdict is against the weight of the evidence. Every order allowing a new trial shall specify of record the ground or grounds on which said new trial is granted.

norms.heading: Motion for new trial when based upon affidavits.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: When a motion for new trial is based upon affidavits they shall be served with the motion. The opposing party has ten days after such service within which to serve opposing affidavits, which period may be extended for an additional period not exceeding twenty days either by the court for good cause shown or by the parties by written stipulation. The court may permit reply affidavits.

norms.heading: When motion for new trial deemed denied.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: If the motion for new trial is not passed on within ninety days after the motion is filed, it is deemed denied for all purposes.

norms.heading: Court may order a new trial, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: Not later than thirty days after entry of judgment, the court of its own initiative may order a new trial for any reason for which it might have granted a new trial on motion of a party, and every order granting a new trial shall specify the grounds therefor.

norms.heading: Abolishment of motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict and motion in arrest of judgment.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: The motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict and the motion in arrest of judgment are hereby abolished and the objections which were heretofore made on such motions may be raised in a motion for a new trial or upon motion filed at the same time as is required for motion for a new trial, praying for appropriate relief in the premises.

norms.heading: Death or other disability of judge — power of substitute.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 510 Trials and Proceedings Before and After Trial

norms.text: If by reason of his going out of office, death, sickness, or other disability, a judge before whom an action has been tried is unable to perform the duties to be performed by the court under this code after a verdict is returned or findings of fact are filed, then any other judge sitting in or assigned to the court in which the action was tried may perform those duties; but if such other judge is satisfied that he cannot perform those duties because he did not preside at the trial or for any other reason, he may in his discretion grant a new trial.

norms.heading: Term "real estate" construed.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The term "real estate", as used in this chapter, shall be construed to include all estate and interest in lands, tenements and hereditaments liable to be sold upon execution.

norms.heading: Judgment defined.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: A "judgment" is the final determination of the right of the parties in the action.
revisor_notes: (1977) Held, failure of judgment entered to mention two of fourteen defendants results in judgment not fully disposing of all parties and judgment is not appealable. Claspill v. Craig (A.), 546 S.W.2d 202.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article confère à la sentence l’autorité de la chose jugée, permet l’exécution provisoire et prévoit sa notification. Le Missouri définit le jugement, prévoit l’exécution d’une sentence soumise à arbitrage et règle la notification et la signification des jugements et actes, mais les textes fournis ne prévoient pas l’exécution provisoire.
correspondences.note_en: The article gives the arbitral award res judicata effect, permits provisional enforcement, and requires notice. Missouri defines a judgment, addresses enforcement of an award submitted to arbitration, and governs notice and service of judgments and papers, but the supplied texts do not provide for provisional enforcement.

norms.heading: Judgment, against whom rendered, effect of — court's powers as to minor or disabled person.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text:
1. Judgment may be given for or against one or more of several plaintiffs, and for or against one or more of several defendants; and it may determine the ultimate rights of the parties on each side, as between themselves, and it may grant to the plaintiff or the defendant any affirmative or other relief to which he may be entitled.

2. If the court determines in any action that a plaintiff or defendant entitled to judgment or other relief is a minor or disabled person, the court may, as part of such judgment, without appointing a conservator, authorize, direct or ratify any transaction necessary or desirable to achieve any security, service or care arrangement meeting the foreseeable needs of such person which is authorized pursuant to the provisions of chapter 475.

3. If the court determines in any action that a plaintiff or defendant entitled to judgment or other relief is a minor or disabled person, the court may, as part of such judgment, without appointing a conservator, authorize, direct or ratify any contract or other transaction relating to such person's financial affairs or involving such person's estate if the court determines that the transaction is in the best interests of such person, provided the transaction is authorized pursuant to the provisions of chapter 475.

norms.heading: Judgment on a counterclaim or cross-claim when court orders separate trials.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If the court orders separate trials as provided in section 510.180, judgment on a counterclaim or cross-claim may be rendered even if the claims of the opposing party have been dismissed or otherwise disposed of.

norms.heading: Judgment of non pros., when entered.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If the plaintiff shall fail to file his replication, or other pleading, within the time prescribed by law or the rules of practice of the court, and to serve the adverse party, or his attorney, with a copy thereof when the same is required, judgment of non pros. shall be given against him.

norms.heading: When set aside.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: The judgment may, for good cause shown, be set aside at any time within thirty days after it is entered, upon such terms as are just.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article renvoie aux articles 1424-8 à 1424-13 pour le réexamen exceptionnel. Les textes du Missouri prévoient plutôt la correction, la remise en cause ou la mise à néant d’un jugement, selon des motifs et délais propres à chaque mécanisme.
correspondences.note_en: The article refers to Articles 1424-8 to 1424-13 for exceptional review. The Missouri texts instead provide mechanisms to correct, reopen, or set aside a judgment, with grounds and time limits specific to each mechanism.

norms.heading: Confession of judgment entered, when.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: A judgment by confession may be entered without action, either for money due or to become due, or to secure any person against contingent liability on behalf of the defendant, or both, in the manner herein prescribed.

norms.heading: Form of confession.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.heading: Defendant identified to court.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Such statement and affidavits shall be filed, and the court shall render judgment for the amount confessed, and cause the same to be entered upon the records, first being satisfied of the identity of the defendant, if present, or, if not present, that he executed the same in writing, and made the affidavit herein required.

norms.heading: Confession by attorney in fact.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: A judgment by confession may also be rendered against any person for a debt owing upon a note, bond or bill of exchange, under his power of attorney therefor, acknowledged as required of deeds of land for record and filed in the court rendering the judgment, at the time of its rendition, together with the note, bond or bill of exchange, and the affidavit of the plaintiff that the debt is bona fide, for a fair and valuable consideration, and owing after allowing all just credits and setoffs.

norms.heading: Interlocutory judgment entered upon default.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If the defendant shall fail to file his answer or other pleading within the time prescribed by law or the rules of practice of the court, and serve a copy thereof upon the adverse party, or his attorney, when the same is required, an interlocutory judgment shall be given against him by default.

norms.heading: When set aside.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Such judgment may, for good cause shown, be set aside at any time before the damages are assessed or final judgment rendered, upon such terms as shall be just.

norms.heading: Judgment interlocutory against only part of the defendants.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: When there are several defendants in a suit, and some of them appear and plead and others make default, an interlocutory judgment by default may be entered against such as make default, and the cause may proceed against the others; but only one final judgment shall be given in the action.
revisor_notes: (2007) Section is invalid as being abrogated by Rule 74.01(b). Hagan v. Buchanan, 215 S.W.3d 252 (Mo.App.W.D.).

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 474 détermine si, en présence de plusieurs défendeurs dont certains ne comparaissent pas, le jugement est réputé contradictoire ou rendu par défaut, selon l’appel possible et la citation à personne. Le Missouri permet un jugement par défaut contre certains défendeurs et la poursuite de l’instance contre les autres, mais ne reprend pas ces critères.
correspondences.note_en: Article 474 determines whether, when several defendants fail to appear, the judgment is treated as adversarial or rendered by default, depending on appealability and personal service. Missouri permits default judgment against some defendants while the action proceeds against the others, but does not reproduce those criteria.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 475 interdit de statuer avant l’expiration du plus long délai de comparution et prévoit en principe un jugement unique contre tous les défendeurs. Le Missouri prévoit un jugement final unique et encadre les décisions concernant seulement certains participants, mais ces textes ne fixent pas le plus long délai de comparution prévu par l’article 475.
correspondences.note_en: Article 475 bars the court from ruling before the longest appearance period expires and generally requires one judgment against all defendants. Missouri provides for one final judgment and regulates decisions involving fewer than all parties, but these provisions do not establish Article 475’s longest appearance period.

norms.heading: Judgment by default, how proceeded on to final judgment.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Whenever an interlocutory judgment shall be rendered for the plaintiff by default nihil dicit, confession, or upon an issue of law, in any suit founded upon a written instrument, or upon a judgment of any court of record, and the demand is ascertained by such instrument or the record of any such judgment, the court shall assess the damages, and final judgment shall be given thereon.

norms.heading: Assessment of damages.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: In all cases of interlocutory judgments not provided for in sections 511.130 and 511.140, the plaintiff may, if he demand it, have a jury to assess his damages. If no jury be demanded the court shall assess the damages, or give the other relief asked in the petition, and final judgment shall be given thereon.
revisor_notes: (2007) Section is invalid as being abrogated by Rule 74.01(b). Hagan v. Buchanan, 215 S.W.3d 252 (Mo.App.W.D.).

norms.heading: Damages not to exceed amount claimed.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: Whenever such interlocutory judgment shall be rendered for the plaintiff, the damages or other relief shall not be other or greater than that which he shall have demanded in the petition, as originally filed and served on defendant; but in any other case, the court may grant him any relief consistent with the case made by the plaintiff and embraced within the issues.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 5 impose au juge de statuer sur toutes les demandes, mais seulement dans leurs limites. RSMo 511.160 interdit d’accorder une réparation supérieure à celle demandée et exige une cohérence avec l’affaire et les questions en litige. La Rule 55.05 exige une demande précisant la réparation sollicitée.
correspondences.note_en: Article 5 requires the court to decide every request, but only within the relief sought. RSMo 511.160 bars relief greater than that demanded and requires consistency with the case and issues. Rule 55.05 requires a demand stating the relief sought.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 464 applique le mécanisme de complément de l’article 463 lorsque le juge statue sur une chose non demandée ou accorde plus que demandé. RSMo 511.160 limite certains dommages ou autres réparations à la demande; Rule 75.01 autorise la modification du jugement dans les trente jours.
correspondences.note_en: Article 464 applies Article 463’s supplementation mechanism when the court rules on an unrequested matter or grants more than requested. RSMo 511.160 limits certain damages or other relief to the amount demanded; Rule 75.01 permits judgment modification within thirty days.

norms.heading: Petition for review, grounds.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: When such interlocutory judgment shall be made and final judgment entered thereon against any defendant who shall not have been summoned as required by this chapter, or who shall not have appeared to the suit, or has been made a party as the representative of one who shall have been summoned or appeared, such final judgment may be set aside, if the defendant shall, within the time herein limited, appear, and by petition for review, show good cause for setting aside such judgment.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 476 ouvre en principe l’opposition contre le jugement rendu par défaut, sauf exclusion expresse. La Rule 74.05 permet de faire annuler un jugement par défaut sur motion, sous conditions et dans un délai maximal d’un an; les autres textes offrent des mécanismes plus limités de remise en cause du jugement.
correspondences.note_en: Article 476 generally allows opposition to a default judgment unless expressly excluded. Rule 74.05 permits a default judgment to be set aside by motion, subject to specified grounds and a one-year maximum, while the other provisions provide narrower forms of relief from judgment.

correspondences.note_fr: L'opposition permet au défaillant de faire rétracter un jugement rendu par défaut. La Rule 74.05 et les §§ 511.170, 511.200 et 511.220 prévoient des mécanismes de remise en cause d'un jugement par défaut, mais avec des conditions, délais et fondements différents.
correspondences.note_en: Opposition allows the defaulting party to obtain retraction of a default judgment. Rule 74.05 and §§ 511.170, 511.200, and 511.220 provide mechanisms to challenge default judgments, but impose different conditions, time limits, and grounds.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 582 permet à un tiers de remettre en cause un jugement afin qu’il soit à nouveau statué en fait et en droit. Le § 511.170 permet surtout au défendeur non assigné ou non comparant de faire annuler le jugement, tandis que la Rule 74.06 prévoit plus généralement un relief contre un jugement, mais principalement au bénéfice d’une partie.
correspondences.note_en: Article 582 allows a nonparty to challenge a judgment so that the case may be decided again on fact and law. RSMo 511.170 permits an unserved or nonappearing defendant to set aside the judgment, while Rule 74.06 provides broader judgment relief but primarily for a party.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article renvoie aux articles 1424-8 à 1424-13 pour le réexamen exceptionnel. Les textes du Missouri prévoient plutôt la correction, la remise en cause ou la mise à néant d’un jugement, selon des motifs et délais propres à chaque mécanisme.
correspondences.note_en: The article refers to Articles 1424-8 to 1424-13 for exceptional review. The Missouri texts instead provide mechanisms to correct, reopen, or set aside a judgment, with grounds and time limits specific to each mechanism.

norms.heading: Bar to petition for review.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If the plaintiff shall, at any time after such final judgment, serve the defendant, within any of the United States or the territories thereof, with notice of the suit and a copy of the judgment thereon, and such defendant shall not, within one year after such service, bring his petition for review, the court, on proof of the service of such notice, shall make an order that the judgment stand absolute.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 586 fixe la durée et le point de départ de la tierce opposition, avec des délais particuliers après notification. Les RSMo 511.180 et 511.190 prévoient des délais de recours après notification ou après le jugement; les Rules 74.03 et 74.06 prévoient aussi des délais liés à la notification et à la remise en cause du jugement, mais pour d’autres recours.
correspondences.note_en: Article 586 establishes limitation periods and triggering events for third-party opposition, including special periods after notice. RSMo 511.180 and 511.190 provide time limits for judgment review, while Rules 74.03 and 74.06 contain notice-related and judgment-relief deadlines for different remedies.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 596 fixe à deux mois le délai du recours en révision à compter de la connaissance de la cause de révision. Les RSMo 511.180 et 511.190 prévoient aussi des délais propres à la petition for review, mais avec des durées, points de départ et effets différents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 596 sets a two-month period for review from knowledge of the ground for review. RSMo 511.180 and 511.190 also provide time limits for a petition for review, but with different durations, triggering events, and effects.

norms.heading: Judgment absolute after three years.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: If such petition for review be not filed within three years after such final judgment is rendered, the same shall stand absolute, whether notice thereof be given or not.

norms.heading: Judgment set aside — contents of petition.

path.label: Title XXXV CIVIL PROCEDURE AND LIMITATIONS
Chapter 511 Judgments

norms.text: No such judgment shall be set aside unless the petition for review shall state the existence of the facts set forth in section 511.170, and that the petition of plaintiff, upon which the judgment complained of was obtained, is untrue in some material matter, setting it forth, or that he has and then had a good defense thereto, setting such defense forth, or both, and then only on condition that the defendant answer or direct a motion to the petition of plaintiff on which the judgment was rendered within a reasonable time, to be ordered by the court. Such petition for review shall be verified by affidavit of the defendant or his attorney of record.

correspondences.note_fr: L'opposition permet au défaillant de faire rétracter un jugement rendu par défaut. La Rule 74.05 et les §§ 511.170, 511.200 et 511.220 prévoient des mécanismes de remise en cause d'un jugement par défaut, mais avec des conditions, délais et fondements différents.
correspondences.note_en: Opposition allows the defaulting party to obtain retraction of a default judgment. Rule 74.05 and §§ 511.170, 511.200, and 511.220 provide mechanisms to challenge default judgments, but impose different conditions, time limits, and grounds.

correspondences.note_fr: L'opposition saisit le même juge afin qu'il statue à nouveau en fait et en droit, le jugement initial ne disparaissant qu'en cas de rétractation. Les textes du Missouri permettent de faire annuler ou réexaminer le jugement par défaut et, selon le § 511.220, de reprendre l'instance comme si le défendeur avait comparu, sans reprendre exactement cette règle.
correspondences.note_en: Opposition returns the matter to the same judge for a new decision on fact and law, with the original judgment surviving unless retracted. Missouri provisions permit default-judgment relief and, under § 511.220, continuation as if the defendant had appeared, but do not reproduce the rule exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’opposition doit exposer les moyens du défaillant. RSMo 511.200 exige que la demande de révision énonce les faits pertinents et la défense valable invoquée, tandis que la Rule 55.26 impose aux motions d’indiquer précisément leurs moyens et le relief demandé.
correspondences.note_en: The opposition must set out the defaulting party’s grounds. RSMo 511.200 requires a review petition to state the relevant facts and meritorious defense, while Rule 55.26 requires motions to state their grounds and requested relief.
